messages.text: Do Not Use
Who is the brave volunteer?
You find a small fortune in treasure!
You see a large hole in the ground.
You stumble into a cave.  Dreams of drying your possessions over a glowing fire warm your thoughts.  Unfortunately, before you can become too comfortable, you see some foreboding signs.
The cave is full of gnawed bones and half-eaten fish heads.  Every inch of the place is littered with animal waste.  A quick look shows the place is uninhabited.
You notice a group of fish-like men approaching the cave.  You could hide and wait them out.  Would you prefer to attack them?
You do not notice the arrival of fish-toting shantilies until it is too late.  Dropping their scaly dinner, they charge you on flapping feet.

A small side cave empties a trickling stream into the cave you are now traveling through.  There is no telling how far back this side cave goes.  It's a tight fit. You would have to move along single file if you continue.  Do you continue?
Since you have to go in single file, what will the marching order be?

You move about 60 feet before it dead ends.  Searching reveals no way out except the way you came.  Turning back, you pass small openings in the wall.  Snakelike creatures squirm out and attack, biting at your heels as you beat a  hasty retreat.

There is a very old-looking shantilie here.  Near death, it slumps on the ground gasping for air.  It has been bitten and is bleeding badly.  Do you try and heal it or do you put it out of its misery?
After the bleeding has been stopped, the beast quickly regains its strength.  It is also quick to attack!
The barkeep thanks you.
You hear the lock click.  It opens.
You fail to pick the lock.
You see a small group of gnaths.  They seem well-armed and able-bodied.  Do you wish to attack them?
You see a group of monsters in the distance.  Do you wish to attack them?
You sense that a group of ruffians has been following you.  Eyeing you with wicked sneers, they obviously believe you are easy pickings.  Do you wish to teach them a lesson?
A trained unit of battle reptiles and a war party of gnaths are being  led by a giant trainer.  Do you wish to attack them?
As you are wading across the moat, an icy grip clamps around your legs like a steel vise.  You have fallen victim to the creatures that guard the moat!
The men who guard the bridge challenge you to show your right of passage.  Since you have none, they demand that you turn back under threat of arms.  Do you continue?
Having crashed the gate, the whole town guard will be after your hide.

The river pours through a large grate in the wall here.  Spacing between the grate's bars is much too small to squeeze through.  However, something very large and powerful must have needed to get through, for now there exists a gaping hole.
Posted on this gate is a placard that reads: "Prison Quarter. No Admittance Without Authorization."
The dead bodies of two dwarves are washed up on shore.  Badly decomposed, they are almost unrecognizable.  A quick search of their bodies reveals nothing of value but a small vial and a map.
You come to a well-stocked but high priced shop.
You come upon a shop.  The sign over the door says, "Ye Ol' Magic Shop".  A great variety of magical items are for sale, but the prices are outrageous.
You come upon a public well.  The water appears cool and clear.  Do you sample some of the water?
Most refreshing!  You refill your water blisters.

You find a secret entrance formed to look like the side of the mountain.  As you open the secret door, stale air belches forth with the grace of a swamp sow.  Beyond lies a steep, sloped tunnel that descends into the very bowels of the earth.
Do you wish to enter this foreboding place now or leave to return at a later date?

You descend for hours down a spiraling passage and emerge into a large underground cavern.  It is overgrown with a spectacular display of flora,  not all of which appears safe to touch.  Denizens of the deep scurry to defend their home.
As you step inside the vault, you hear a soft wispy sound.  You ply an ear to determine its source and find that the vault is not completely unoccupied.
After defeating the horrible guardians, you witness an amazing sight.  A magic mouth appears before you and cries,  "You have killed my pets!  You shall pay with your very souls!"
Before you stands a great iron door set into the very rock of the cavern.  A large keyhole exists seven feet from the ground.  This door must have been made for someone extremely tall.
You come to a chest.  It does not appear to be locked.  Do you wish to open it?
This underground river runs very shallow and slow.  It appears to be safe and easy wading into the cave for quite some distance.  Do you wish to enter and see where it leads?
A hob goblin patrol is moving in the distance.  Do you wish to waylay them?

You enter Castle Fairlawn.  The steward announces you to his lordship, Sir Bradwick, who tells this tale.  "Hundreds of years ago a mighty war was waged.  The men allied with the dwarves and elves to repel a foul invasion.
The foe was the greatest assembly of evil folk ever known and was led by the wicked race of giants.  As you know from legend, the goodly races won the day and drove the giants from our fair land.
Alas, nothing good can last forever. The giants have returned to vie once again for domination of our land.  We would drive them back again, but things are not as they once were.

The dwarves have become a race of hermits and want nothing to do with the outside world.  They would be just as happy to see the rest of the world fall.  The elves are no better.  They have retreated to Chastity Wood.

Attempts to convince the dwarves and elves to aid us have ended in hot-blooded feuds.  Unfortunately, each blames the other for the giants' return.  I believe no one is to blame.  We must set aside these petty accusations in order to fight our common foe.

However, I am in the minority."  King Bradwick briefly summarizes past and present events before explaining the present tactical position of the human nation.  "During the great wars, the giants beset our land from a set of three citadels.

These citadels have stood empty for many years.  Fearing evil may still dwell there, no one ever dared to enter.  Now there are signs that the giants have returned and taken up refuge once again within these iron-clad citadels.

Provokingly, the giants have constructed four military outposts along the border of what long ago served as the front battle line.  These foul outposts have been crowded with evil folk bound to obey their bidding.

One such outpost is a scant distance from the town of Crystalmire.  The giants and their evil minions raid these outlying towns and cause general havoc.  At this very moment, they are making preparations and plan to lay siege to these very walls.

All the dukes and barons of the surrounding lands have been summoned by me to aid us in our struggle.  They may arrive too late.  We cannot count on the dwarves and elves to suddenly come to their senses.
If you help us defeat this scourge that has befallen us, I will reward you handsomely.  My steward here can provide you with all the information we possess in regard to our enemy's positions."

The steward leads you into a side chamber where he tells you the following information.  "As my liege referred to earlier, the giants have constructed four military outposts from which they send out raiding parties.

Spy reports show that the first outpost houses ogres.  The second contains hob goblins and the third, gnaths.   The fourth outpost houses minotaur.  Mysteriously, we don't know why the minotaurs are presently aiding the giants.

The minotaurs may be unwilling participants.  We do not know for certain.  This group as a whole is known as the iron foursome.  In addition to these vast garrisons, they have many goblin parties employed as patrols.

It will be no picnic. Your specific mission is to attempt to destroy the enemy fortifications, determine who is behind the return of the giants and slay them.  Report all accomplishments in destroying enemy fortifications to Baron McReese.

I must be off to attend to my duties.  May Shalem smile upon you, now and always."  The king retreats from the room.  A great adventure lies before you.  It will be dangerous, if not impossible.  The steward shows you to the door.
You converse with various officials about your adventures.

You enter Castle Clairmon, home of Lord Oswald.  Treated as special guests, you are shown to the chambers of Lord Oswald.  "You appear to be an adventuresome lot.  I have need of such a group, for I have lost something very dear to me."

"Under King Bradwick's orders, I have sent delegates to the dwarves in an attempt to obtain their allegiance in the war before it is too late.  My delegates have returned with both good and bad news.  The good news is that the dwarves have agreed to help.

"Unfortunately, they will not swear allegiance until I return an item of great antiquity and power - the Axe of Ashblet.  Amongst the dwarven clans, it is said that Reorx himself smiles upon those that hold the Axe and pledge their allegiance to him."

"Two dwarves in my employ were sent on a quest to find the Axe.  I have not heard from them for some time now, and I fear their demise.  If you could pick up their trail or find the Axe yourselves, I would be in your debt."

After some idle prattle revealing little of importance, he finally provides you a with possible lead. "My hirelings were fond of dwarven ale.  The only place I know that serves such dreck is the Glowing Coal Inn.  Ask the bartender if he knows anything."

He bids you farewell, and you are escorted to the chamber door.  You ask the footman for directions to the Glowing Coal Inn.   He states that it is a very small inn and not easy to find.  The footman draws you a map.

"Heard the other day that Brystol Wynn, a little village just south of here, was turnin' into a real ghost town.  All the folks been packin' up and movin' to the city.  Plumb shame, I say.  Church is gettin' more needy folks than it can  feed."
"There's been talk that Duke Smeltriv is comin' to town today.  Looks like the trouble with them pesky giants is at an end."
"Two suspicious fellas, dwarf types, been pokin' around.  Kept whispering about the town watering hole like it was someplace special."

"Fella was in here the other day sayin' he'd seen trolls marchin' this way.  Said the whole pack of filthy vermin were bein' herded by a couple of giants.  Well, I think it ain't nothin' but a crazy rumor."
"You ask a lot of questions.  How 'bout a little dwarven ale?  I'm tryin' to run a business here."

You overhear a dwarf sobbing in the corner, "I told Chipper not to go lookin' for it.  He never did have any sense.  Always sayin' Reorx left the great Axe on earth to temper it for awhile.  He's just plumb stupid, and he's gone and got himself lost."
You see a couple of barhands both eyeing you appreciatively.  You have obviously caught their attention.  One comes closer to you but does not say anything of interest.
A gruff-looking dwarf spills some ale on your boots.  He apologizes but then proceeds to belch in your face.
A crude-looking map has been etched into the old wooden tabletop.  It portrays a well located adjacently to a small lake.

This is the shack of a gnath commander. Accompanied by several of his underlings, it is obvious that he is not happy to see you.   He also appears uninterested to participate in a mutual exchange of ideas.

Your search of the hut reveals nothing of  interest or value.  The paper covered table contains information regarding routine patrols.  Nothing is out of the ordinary.  The commander appears to be new to the job and not very trustworthy.

You search the hut.  A small iron box contains a scroll testifying to a secret pact uniting gnaths and ogres together.  Their agreement states, "We will both attack the minotaurs on the appointed day, and they will no longer be the favored..."
The ogres and the gnaths are jealous of the minotaurs' status amongst the giants.
Your attempt to gain entrance to this hut was a horrible mistake.  It is bulging with sweaty bodies standing 7 feet tall.  Suddenly, they charge you without any warning.
This barracks is occupied by a few gnaths.  They are currently off duty and greatly displeased about having to dispatch your puny force on their time off.
You approach the gate surrounding the outpost's headquarters.  It's heavily guarded.  A hailstorm of arrows and flaming pitchballs pelts downward as soon as you move within bowshot.
You are pinned down from missile fire when the gate opens swiftly.  Howling bodies belch forth and bolt in your direction.  The gate slams shut once again.
Nearing the end of your search, you discover a wooden door cleverly built into the floor.  Behind it is a tunnel that leads downward.  Do you wish to follow the tunnel?
The tunnel leads to a small opening in the surface.  You are now within the great wall guarding the main tower.
You enter the tunnel leading back to the gnath commander's hut.
Shouts reporting intruders ring out.  Most guards patrolling minor entrances to the tower are called away to form search parties.  Luck has granted a temporary easy entrance to the tower.
This cell is empty.

A human wretch lies imprisoned in this cell.   In such poor health, he could never survive the walk back to civilization.  Do you kill him with mercy and save him from  endless cruel torture or release him to attempt an escape on his own?

Stepping through the holding area's doorway, he stumbles headlong into a group of gnaths standing in the hallway.  He prays one last time to his god as blood and spittle fall from his lips.  With ugly enjoyment, the gnaths callously kill the poor soul.

However, the gnaths have more important duties than wasting their time on some poor, useless wretch.  They are determined to discover who is responsible for the releasing of prisoners.  Rushing in to investigate, they find you.

The remains of several humanoids lie stacked in the corner.  Their exact race is impossible to tell.  Presumably, they served as food for the creatures secured in this cell.  Unexpectedly, the creatures rush you in an escape attempt.

The creatures appear to be from the nether world.  They are bristling with fangs and claws, they have four arms and are heading right for you.  Do you allow them to pass or do you want to end their existence in the Realmz?
A stout, but unlocked door.  You smell a familiar scent of confined and decaying bodies.  This must be some kind of prison or holding pen.
This door is also quite sturdy.  However, it was designed to be an obstacle for those  inside.  You easily open the simple latch system.

Two dwarves are chained to the wall.  Although the chains are rusty, the enfeebled dwarves are unable to break them.  You detect the weakest link and pry the chains apart.  They thank you gratefully and exit out the door.

This door is unlocked.  As you peer inside, you see two large gnaths sitting slouched at a table.  Gaming bones and a pitcher of cheap wine litter the table.   Assigned to keep watch over the rabble in the cells, the guards presently sit fast asleep.

You note that a large rope is suspended from the ceiling.  It dangles close to a guard's hand.  On the table next to the gaming bones, lay a few gems and a set of jailer's keys.  Do you wish to try and pilfer the items without waking the guards?
Success!  You furtively pocket the gems and keys without incident.

Your foot accidentally kicks a small pebble. It rolls under the table and hits a guard's foot.  He cracks open a bloodshot eye, sees you, and kicks his partner's foot to awaken him.  Realizing that they're outnumbered, they attempt to make a deal.
If you leave now, they promise not to sound the alarm until you have left.  Do you attack them?
As you rush them, one pulls the rope and sounds a gong.  They strive to defend themselves until help can arrive.

Before the blood ceases to flow from the dead, a detachment of troops arrives to investigate the alarm.  The spectacle of their dead comrades incites them to immediately engage you in an all-out brawl.
Inside, you hear the muffled reply of two dwarves.  They explain that they're  chained to the wall and need your help to break out.
The door bursts open in a shower of splintered boards.
An immense growl reverberates throughout the room.  The creatures inside are not happy to be there.
This door is locked.
You are certain that there is no trap.
You do not detect a trap.
The door is too strong.
You have entered the kitchens.  Two gnaths are busy supervising some goblin cooks.  Upon seeing you, the gnaths command the cooks to take up arms and fight.
A few gnaths discover you wandering about.
Smells drift from kitchen pots and  permeate the air with a foul odor.  You discover old crates containing stolen iron rations.  They must be from a merchant train that never reached its destination.

The evening meal, a ogre sits chained against a corner wall.  Frightened beyond belief, the ogre begs you to free him.  You loosen the chains.   He thanks you profusely and vows that at some future date he will repay your kindness.
Just before leaving, he reveals the following information.  "I was taken prisoner three days ago.  In that time, the leader of this foul band boasted of his evil actions."

"Feeling certain of my ultimate fate, he joyfully recounted his evil deeds both past and present.  My spirit waned, and I felt these hideous secrets would weigh heavily upon my soul until death's release. Yet, I suspect much of it was inventions and lies.

"I was bound and dragged throughout the upper level of this fortress for two days.  As a result, I know the floor plan quite well."  Before slipping away, he thanks you once again and provides you with a map of the upper floor.
You enter a large barracks.  Many troops are sleeping soundly.  Guards on watch immediately call them to arms.
This barracks appears to have lain empty for some time.  All the doors are capable of being bolted from the inside. You could rest easily here without being disturbed.

You have found the armory.  Most of the equipment is fashioned for 7 foot gnaths.  Many items appear to be stolen.   Nearby towns and merchants' wagon trains are obviously being raided on a frequent basis.
Just as you open the door to this long narrow room, you hear movement at the far end.  In such dim lighting, it is impossible to discern what could have produced the noise.

This is a storage room for dried provisions in case of siege.  Crates and piles of ripped sacks are scattered about.  Gnaw markings reveal that rodents may have gotten into the provisions.  A barrel of fermented wine stands in the corner.
You open the lid on the wine.  The strong, pungent odor nearly knocks you off your feet.
You feel dizzy for a moment, but then it passes.
Your guts begin to churn, and you feel ready to retch.  Horrified, you suspect the wine has been poisoned.

The wine spreads along the floor soaking nearby provisions.  You hear a large animal thrashing about.  It soon stops.  Hidden under some crates and sacks, you  discover a giant rat covered in wine.  It is quite dead.

After moving some provisions, you inadvertently stumble upon a hole in the wall.  It is just large enough for someone to crawl inside, but they would have very limited movement.  Does someone want to crawl into the hole?

Inside the tunnel, the odor of dung and urine assaults your nose.  Soon the tunnel grows too small to continue.  Numerous giant rats attack, bite and scratch.  As you back out, you find a small gem stuck in some grime.
With the aid of the wine the flames burn fiercely, you can hear giant rats squeal in pain.   They burn alive until nothing but ash is left behind.

In this room, a giant uncomfortably sits on a hard bunk waiting impatiently.   When you enter, he jumps up and declares angrily, "Finally! I must be escorted to Jekar at once.  I have been waiting for over an hour. "

He immediately senses your confusion and becomes suspicious.  Your inability to answer a few probing questions reveals that you do not know Jekar and that you are an intruder of the outpost.  The giant gives a deafening bellow and rushes out the door.

You deftly search the giant's belongings, and discover that he was delivering new orders to the gnath garrison commander.  Attacks are to be stepped up on the already beleaguered outlying human villages just before a planned fatal all-out attack.
You have entered a cloak room.  Many of the cloaks are shabby and falling apart.  However, two seem very well-made.

This room is very large.  Muddy footprints cross the floor.  Their tracks lead back and forth from this door to another door on the far side of the room.  Miscellaneous pieces of equipment lie about in various states of disrepair.
This room is strangely ornate, considering that the occupant is a powerful gnath.  The garrison commander is also unusual in size.  He is quite small - only slightly over 6 feet tall.

Such a short commander must live by his wit as well as his brawn if he expects to remain in charge.  Bursting into his office,  you find him sitting in a high-backed chair with his hands crossed.   It appears as if your visit is not wholly unexpected.

"Welcome!  I heard the commotion outside and have been expecting your arrival for some time now.  You have caused quite a stir around here.  I will have to discipline my commanders for not apprehending you earlier."
"No matter.  Having got this far, your presence here warrants discussion."  He gestures to some chairs with his hand.  "Please, sit down."  Do you sit and listen to what he has to say?

"Very well.  If that is your decision, do not waste any more of my valuable time."  He hurls a glass ball at your feet.   Abruptly, it erupts into tall spurts of green flame.  Smoke chokes your lungs.  Gnaths rush in to aid the garrison commander.

At the death of the garrison leader, total chaos erupts.  The various commanders fight for total control of the outpost.  Their foolish lust for power causes their own downfall.  The gnaths no longer pose a threat as you collect all treasure.

You feel a growing sense of unease as his voice rambles on endlessly.  Polite mannerisms cannot hide cold, calculating eyes. It suddenly dawns on you that he is stalling for time, when you are interrupted by a knock on the door.
You quickly deal the commander a lethal blow to the head and throw open the door.  You are surprised by a group of young gnaths.  Upon seeing their dead father, they seek to take revenge.

They reluctantly agree and leave.  In a desperate attempt to summon help, the garrison commander makes a break for the door.  You quickly slay him with a blade across the throat.  He slips to the floor in a bloody heap.
On the garrison commander, you find a small pouch of green glass marbles.  They radiate a strange aura and appear magical in nature.
You collect the items worn by the commander.  You find nothing else of interest in his office except for three potions.
This room is teeming with garrison troops preparing for a patrol.
This is the garrison commander's personal chambers.  The room is filled with comfortable looking furniture and several chests.  None of the chests hold anything you would want.
The garrison commander's sleeping quarters.  The bed sports a fine down mattress and thick quilts made from humanoid hair woven into artistic designs.

In the corner of the room is a large water basin.  As you move it aside, you reveal a small hidden chamber in the stand.  You suspected the garrison commander was capable of casting magic and now you have proof.
At first glance, this room seems empty.  As you are about to leave you smell a funny odor.  It smells like honey and it is definitely coming from this room.

This room is an old staging area for patrols.  Currently it is empty and does not seem to be used very often.  The door is capable of being bolted shut in times of strife.  You could easily rest here undisturbed.
This room appears empty.  You feel a slight breeze even though you have closed the door behind you.  There must be another way in or out of this room.

Upon entering this chamber, you notice a  ladder leading to a small guard tower at the summit of the outpost.  You hear several gnath voices above.  Do you wish to ambush the guards or leave them alone?

As you poke your head into the guard room, you are seen by one of the guards.  He pulls a chain that rings a gong and quickly hacks at the point man.  The force of the blow breaks the ladder you are standing on and you all tumble back down.
You must move up the ladder single file.  Who will lead the way?

The guards throw a trap door over the hole and secure themselves inside.  You here them shouting an alarm to some gnaths outside the outpost to be on the lookout for intruders.  This will make moving surreptitiously very difficult.

This is a small stable.  There are many horses inside, but you do not see any saddles.  You also have not noticed any gnaths riding horses since you entered the outpost.  You speculate that the horses are being used as livestock.
Do you wish to set them free and spare them from the gnath's cookfires?
The sight of all the horses running loose causes an uproar amongst the gnaths.  It will now be more difficult to move about surreptitiously.
These large buildings store dried foodstuffs and large-scale equipment.  Do you wish to set the warehouses on fire in an effort to hinder the gnaths' ability to wage war on the humans?

Gnaths rush to put out the flames.  You barely escape without being seen.  This will make it difficult to move about surreptitiously.  However, it will be a while before the gnaths can replenish their supplies. This will buy the humans precious time.

This room is patrolled by a large group of gnaths.  They attack with uncommon bravado.  You suspect that you are very close to the outpost commander.  The gnaths are of better than average skill and appear to be bodyguards.
There is a large force of gnaths guarding the gate.  They obviously expect some type of attack.
Never too bright, the goblins only guard the gates of this flea trap with a small force.

The goblins are low on supplies and are packed into this crude hut like sardines.  Two or three goblins squabble over each cot.  Although it's a humorous scene to an outsider, tempers are riding so high someone's throat could get slit over this issue.

One monstrous brute of a goblin sits alone and unbothered in the midst of this struggle for bunks.  He lazily lies back sucking the marrow from some bones.  Suddenly, he sees you and immediately bellows orders for his comrades to take you by force.
Six goblins of some considerable girth are playing bones in the center of this small hut.  They are shouting and arguing so loud, they did not hear you enter.  Do you wish to ambush them?

You happen upon a hut full of loudly snoring goblins.  With all their noise, nothing but a shattering earthquake could wake them.  You can hardly believe how lazy and worthless these goblin scum are.  No wonder their outpost is so small.
Do you wish to wake up these ignorant fools for a fair fight, or would you rather set the hut on fire and let them fry in their sleep?

You wake the goblins and back away to make room as they begin to pour out the door.  There are a lot more than you had thought.  Due to a shortage of bunks and space, many had been sleeping under others' bunks.
The gods of fair play smile on you.

The goblins begin to squeal like stuck pigs as they burn alive.  A few burst from the sides of the straw hut, but the burning straw clings to them and hastens their death.  Many small fuzzy animals will sleep easy tonight.

The flames alert a small goblin patrol force outside the walls.  Rushing in, they see you gloating over the dead.  Horrified, the small patrol sizes you up and drinks in the terrible scene.  They quickly turn and flee.  Do you wish to pursue?

Their puny legs are pumping at a furious rate as they rush out of the gate.  As you clear the gate, you are enveloped by missile fire from your flanks.  The little buggers are smarter than you thought.

You come upon one of the most repulsive sights you have ever seen.  A four foot goblin that must weigh over three hundred pounds is sitting inside an unusually well-built hut.  Every inch of this sick creature is warty green blubber.

Having witnessed your coming, he is now huddled in the corner shivering in terror. Fine robes adorn his body, and many jeweled rings decorate his fat fingers. The rings must be quite old, for the fat on his fingers will allow only one method of  removal.

He observes you eyeing his jewelry and guesses your thoughts.  "Please, please! Oh, great warriors! Don't hurt me.  My name is Thoode, and I can be of great assistance to you.  Spare me, and I shall give you all that you ask!"

The foul creature grovels at your feet, wallowing in self-pity.  You view him with disdain.  Your eyes speak of extinction. He offers to tell you a great secret if you spare his unworthy carcass.  Do you agree, or do you cut up his fingers for the loot?

Before you can move, he swallows something.  He begins to gag and tremble. Foam spews from between clenched teeth.  He is now missing one of his front teeth.  He spits a stream of the poisonous, reeking foam into your face.
He suddenly pitches forward.  Ribs crack as his bulk slams the hard ground.  You quickly relieve him of his prized possessions.  If only he would have prized his life as much.
He kicks some dirt away from a small box  buried in the dirt.  "It's in there, fine people.  What you seek is in there."      Who digs it up?

He pulls the top off the worm-eaten box, plucks out a vial, and holds it aloft.  "Hold, stupid fools!  If you don't, I will smash this vial of soul-stealing at your feet.  None have felt its effects and lived!"  Do you rush him or let him go?
You quickly put an end to his miserable life.
The vial turns out to be a bottle of harmless lilac water.  The box contains another empty bottle and some worthless documents.
As you are digging up the old box, Thoode slips out the door and disappears.  The box contains some magical items.
A large structure that houses a company of minotaur soldiers.  One in particular stands out as the commander and pushes his way to the front of his troops.  He begins to make ready for battle.
This gate is guarded by a medium-sized contingent of ogres.

Made of rough lumber, this large building is constructed very poorly.  The boards have been nailed together in a very crude manner.  By peering through the gaps, you can easily make out a huge ogre surrounded by many of his fellows.

The leader is gloating over a human female.  His prisoner is tied down to the top of a table.  Saliva dribbles from his massive fangs as he laughs at her predicament.  He is poking her with a sharpened stick and drawing blood.
Do you wish to rush in and rescue her?
The woman appears to be unconscious.  Do you wish to cut her loose?
The moment she is free, she jumps up from the table and points at one of the dead ogres.  She begins to chant a magic spell.  Do you attack her before she finishes?
She completes the spell, and several of the ogres rise.  She points to you and commands them to attack.
The shoreline grows too cluttered to continue.  You are forced to turn back.

The footing amid this terrain is tricky and unsafe.  Some of your party slip on the slime-covered rocks, fall in the stagnant water, and gulp down its nasty swill.  Slipping and sliding, you're finally able to crawl your way out.
A temple dedicated to the worship of Triby, goddess of the whispering winds.  A regal-looking man approaches and offers to perform services...for a fee.
You discover a cleverly concealed tunnel.   Several prisoners must have worked together to dig a means of escape.

You come to a dead-end.  A large cave-in has collapsed the tunnel.  You smell the rancid odor of decomposing flesh wafting from the rubble.  Several hands, clawed and otherwise, protrude from the debris.
A daring escape has been foiled by mother nature.  Do you wish to dig the bodies out?

Digging slowly, you begin to uncover large bodies in various stages of decomposition.  The bodies closer to the surface are worse than those below.  The sickly flesh peels off in your hands as you pull on arms and legs.
The rancid stench is overwhelming. Suddenly, you are stricken with horror. The pile of bodies is infested by a host of carrion grubs.  Within seconds, they begin to dig into your flesh.
You will surely die, unless you can find a way to quickly rid yourself of these foul parasites.

Your digging has unearthed the body of a Truscan guard.  His body bears a paper inscribed in the king's own hand.  It reads, "Once released, you are hereby commanded to form a band that carries out the king's secret bidding.  The future of...

the entire kingdom is at stake.   Your first mission is to create havoc in the town of Bristol.  You must make it appear as if giants have done this grave deed.  I fear that the people do not understand the gravity of our present situation...
If we fail to develop a strong desire amongst the people to fight and defend our land, it will be too late.  The giants will destroy and conquer us all. "

Do you take the scroll, confront the king, and denounce his unscrupulous methods of rallying the people?  OR  Do you decide that you would rather not get involved in this potentially sticky situation?

You storm into the king's audience chamber to confront him about his unlawful attacks on the village of Bristol.  As you lambaste the king in front of the entire court, the veins in his neck begin to bulge with anger.

"How dare you question my authority? The manner in which I rule my kingdom is not your affair.  You shall rue the day you crossed me.  Guards, throw these fools into the dungeons!  The beasts living within shall devour them."  You are quickly seized.

As you are being forced from the chamber, some guards question the king about what to do with your equipment.  He orders the guards to halt as he reconsiders the situation.  "I will give you a choice.  You may become my dungeon prisoners or...
if you can escape the pit of pain alive, I will allow you to keep your equipment and return to my service."  You have no choice but to accept this opportunity to redeem yourselves.
You are forcibly escorted to the pit of pain.  Not allowed to make any preparations beforehand, the guards rudely thrust you into the chamber to manage your escape.

You escape the pit of pain.  The king is informed of your success, and you are summoned before him.  "Your ability to escape the pit of pain attests to your mighty strength.  Many have tried and  failed.  I had promised that if you escaped...

You discover the remains of victims who never escaped this dreadful pit.  They appear to have been clawed to death by monstrous beasts.  Most of their possessions have been torn to shreds.  However, a few items remain intact.
Do you wish to take the equipment from the dead?  OR  Do you dig them a proper grave?
You have chosen poorly.

The guards remove your blindfolds.  You are standing in a large cavern.  The kings' guards wish you luck.  They disappear around a bend in the rocks.  Your presence begins to attract a cacophony of creatures.

Your eyes are drawn to a corpse.  The manner of dress suggests he once served as a king's aide.  A scroll on his body reads, "If you vow to uphold the king's will, you shall be granted freedom.  Your first mission is to attack the village of Bristol...
You must make it look like giants have attacked the village."  Further reading shows that this is part of the king's plan to raise public emotions in order to rally the people against the giants.
Once formidable, the gates of this mighty prison now hang open on rusted hinges.   A great shifting of the earth has caused the hinges to pop their retaining pins and allowed prisoners to escape.
The king's steward listens to your progress.

"Your foolish tongue is pardoned, and you are now reinstated to my service.  You are hereby forgiven for all past wrongdoing. Go.  Act as champions to my cause.  Time is short, and you must complete your quest."

One of his aides pulls you aside.  You are quietly warned not to cross the king a second time, "The king has been unusually generous.  Those that double-cross him are beheaded by the king's personal axeman and put on public display."

Pain shoots up your arms and legs.  It feels like liquid fire racing through your veins.  A sudden darkness follows.  When you regain your senses, you find yourself standing a short distance away from where you were before.
You enter a large cave.  It is strangely quiet.  The unusual lack of sound is eerie. Your skin is crawling, and you feel like a bundle of nerves.
You enter the pit of pain.
The chest erupts into a ball of flame.
The loud explosion has produced laughter from the gods.   Numerous creatures that inhabit the caves are drawn to the ruckus.
Small shuffling sounds come from behind the door.  An unexpected bolt of magical energy streaks from out of nowhere.
The door swings open on rusty hinges.
As you walk by this hut, a peculiar growl pierces through its walls.  The noise sounds partly human and partly...  You're not altogether sure.  Do you step inside?

You burst through the door and see the back of an old woman.  She spins around to face you.  She is foaming at the mouth.  Gnashing her toothless gums together, she bites air and produces even more.  Your feet have been sprayed with this white froth.
Before you can react, she launches herself at you in mad fury.  Do you cut her down like a rabid dog?

You deal a swift blow and make a quick end to her life.  It's doubtful that she had enough self awareness left to recognize her own insanity.  A quick search reveals nothing of interest or value in the tiny hut.

The town patrol shows up.  You explain what happened.  The guards inform you that she had been a lowly nursemaid to the old king.  Long ago she had acted as an indiscreet lover and brought disgrace upon the current king's father.

She was banished and a social outcast for many years.  Recently, the king had pardoned her and had ordered a search to be conducted.  He declared her sins forgiven and bequeathed her gold for her many years of devoted service.

The woman had no surviving relatives.   Because you were with the deceased at the time of death, you shall inherit everything.  This is the law of the kingdom.  The guards give you a large sack of coins.
She rushes past you in a fit of rage.  She sprays foam and mucous all over you as she passes.

You find the dead body of the mad woman from the hut.  It is lying in a grassy clump and her face is entirely covered by foam and mucous.  The grotesque sight makes you bend over and dress your boots with your breakfast.
She is clutching a small sack in one hand.  You pry it from her stiff fingers and find a gloomy-looking ring inside.  It looks worthless.
This is the grave site of the former king.  It is well maintained and surrounded by beautiful bouquets of flowers.

You stand over the old king's grave site. The ground begins to rumble.  As you watch in amazement, a wisp of smoke seeps upwards from the ground and materializes into the spectral shape of the former king.
Your attempt has enraged the ghostly figure.  His eyes flash brighter.  He begins to quickly lose patience with you.

"All these years my soul has wandered.  I am unable to rest in peace.  I command you to give me that which was once rightfully mine - my gift to my long lost beloved.  If you refuse, you shall join me in this accursed state of eternal unrest."

"Because you will not give me what is rightfully mine, you must pay for your greedy piracy."  Mumbling a few ancient words, the former king's tremulous spirit solidifies into a solid form.   The soil around you opens up into a mass of zombies.

"Thank you, fine people.  I sensed your inner goodness."  The king places the ring on his wispy finger.  The ring's gloom dissipates into the king's smoky form.  As the gloom disappears, another shadowy form...

comes into being next to the king.  It is the mad woman from whom you originally acquired the ring.  Now she is breathtakingly beautiful.  The two kiss and fade away.  The ring falls to the grass shining like the sun.
The wispy figure grasps his head and screams in pain.  "Fools, you have damned me to an eternal hell!"  The figure fades from view.

A wispy looking figure appears before you and stares at you with intense pulsating eyes.  Standing on the grave of the former king, you have come face-to-face with his ghost.  "Give me that which was once mine and rightfully belongs to my one true love."
A sign over the tavern reads, "Glowing Coal Inn.  House of Fine Dwarven Spirits."  Patrons are few, and most are dwarves.  The pungent smell of dwarven ale fills the room.
This grave has been robbed recently.  The body that was once resting here in peace is now resting here in pieces.  Do you wish search the grave site?

You find two silver coins in the pocket of the corpse's tattered robe.  They are unlike any other silver coins you have ever seen.  Written in very small runes are the words, "Wishing you well"  Do you wish to take them?

You are about to dismiss this hole, when  something about it catches your interest.  Someone has gone out of their way to force a large boulder inside it, for no apparent reason.  Two odd indentations have been chiseled into the boulder's surface.
What is it that you wish to do?
That has no apparent effect.
You do not detect anything out of the ordinary.
Nothing seems to happen.
Nothing happens.

You discover some backpacks at the bottom of the pond.  You bring them to the surface and inspect the contents.  The  clothing has been customized to fit dwarves.  Except for a couple special items, they appear common and ordinary.

Curiously, there are no personal items of any kind.  You wonder if they were very poor.  Maybe they were robbed.  The items you do find seem to provide few clues as to their identity.  Funny though.  If they did have equipment it must be here somewhere.
This is an old abandoned shack.  Inside, everything is coated with a thick dust.  Not even homeless paupers seem to want to inhabit this place.

This place reeks of body odor so foul, it would make a sweating mud devil gag in disgust.  The former occupant must have  produced this hellish, putrid stink.  You cannot even imagine how bad it must have been when the stench was still fresh.
You conduct a quick search and find an enormous suit of plate armor hidden in a wooden cabinet.  It shines as if it were still new.
The water tastes a little salty.
Most refreshing.  You refill your water blisters.
The water tastes kind of sweet.
The water has a metallic silvery taste.
You toss the two silver coins into the well and hear them splash into the water below.  Looking down, you see the reflections of your faces dancing about on the ripples.  Soon the ripples fade away.
The reflection is not what it was before.  The blue sky has been replaced with the glow of a city in flames.  Children are standing in the street.  Tears flow down their mud-streaked cheeks.

Death cries and wails of despair ring out. All-out attacks are occurring on this town that is presently quite peaceful.  Giants standing 20 feet or more in height, attack citizens and warriors throwing their bodies about like tent pegs.
You have been made privy to an evil portent.   Future tragedy may strike this fair city.  A faint voice cries, "Seek ye the Anvil of Pain.  It is your one greatest hope of salvation...
For on its surface you must destroy your salvation. Failure to do so will invite a withering death as sure as the sun shall always rise."
As soon as the voice fades, the reflection returns to normal.

Upon the creatures death, it's body turns to stone in the flash of an eye.  Any weapon in contact with the beast is frozen solid within.  You will have to use another weapon until you can retrieve this one from the creatures body.

The local inn.  Once a happy-go-lucky town, Brystol Wynn is now a somber place.  Maggot folk have conducted many raids on Brystol.  Most residents have suffered over deaths or mysterious disappearances of close friends and relatives in recent months.

A towns person speaks, "Brystol Wynn was always such an open place.  We welcomed all, and now it has proven to be our downfall.  There are no longer enough warriors to defend the town, and I plan on moving to the city."

Franklin told me that he knows the location of a secret cave. Travel to the southeast village wall, you will find a group of rocks.  The Imhotep Outcropping is a group of rocks just south of this group.  The cave is located on its northeastern side.

Steven Furbough is a foolish one.  He babbles continuously about an ancient sword called the Giant Slayer.  He claims it's our only hope for successfully conquering the giants.  Supposedly, it's hidden in a cave located at the Imhotep Outcropping.
It's better for you, if you don't ask so many questions.  Nosy people have a habit of getting killed.
Legends say the Anvil of Pain was used solely to destroy magical relics.  The Anvil was forged by the gods of ORDER.   ORDER despised magic because it caused chaos where ORDER should rule.

I wish the news was good, my fine friends.  Alas, it is most grim.  The good king cannot spare any troops to help defend the town from these infernal attacks.  He is presently marshaling every troop to his side in preparation for a great battle.

I know little about this.  I am but a simple man in complex times.   I do know that if the king cannot protect his own city, we cannot hope that he will be able to defend us either.  People are packing what few possessions they have and are fleeing.

The head elder speaks, "I heard of a great battle between the king's men and a band of vermin at Wispy Falls Way.  The king's men put up a valiant fight but lost the battle due to their commander's poor strategic planning."
You have found a secret passage in a group of rocks.  This group is known as the Imhotep Outcropping by Brystol Wynn locals.   A small dark cave leads in a southwesterly direction.

I fear that the king is not totally aware of how much danger he's in.  Many of the minor nobles are discontented and disagree with his command decisions.  If things stew for much longer, he might have to deal with a mutinous uprising among the men.

The local priests are pleased with your generosity.  "Bless you and your unselfish giving.  There are so many homeless children.  This fine day they shall all receive a hot meal.  May the gods smile upon you and make your journey a safe one."
The local priests are pleased with your generosity.  "Gods be praised!  Your place in the promised land is assured.  Go with our blessings, my children."
The local priests are pleased with your generosity, "You are most kind.   We shall cast healing on you to help you gain strength for the long roads ahead."

"Hmmm, let me see...  As I recall, it was a little south of here.  Some gnaths attacked a small wagon train.  If memory serves correctly, it was a short ways due south of the southern gate.  I believe it was near the shepherds' watering hole."

You approach the area where you believe the last raid occurred.  Upon your arrival, you bear witness to an unnerving sight.  The culprits of the previous raid have returned to the scene of their crime.  You see a large group of gnaths...

camped around a fire.  A large, crude hut has been erected nearby.  The raiding party's leader must be quartered there.  Do you wish to ambush them by surprise, perhaps improving your odds of success?
You storm the camp.  The gnaths quickly form into squads.  There are two squads of veterans and two squads of younger troops.  Three massive hill giants lead the squads and bark orders.
It was a difficult battle, but you are victorious.  Most of the take consists of  fairly common items.  However, the hut contains several odd items of interest.

The village elders live in this small group of shacks.  Old and frail, they depend on the village as a means of support.  If  attacks on the village continue, their livelihood will be jeopardized.  With this on their mind, they request a favor from you.
"One time when they were practicin' bugle calls, the vermin stormed out of a cave and attacked.  That might be a good way to draw 'em out.  I'll draw you a map and give you a horn for blowin'.

You blow heartily into the ivory horn.  A loud bellow, like a water buffalo in heat, issues forth.  You continue to blow.  Eager to put an end to the wailing, large bodies begin to rush forth from the cave.

On this day a great evil has been put to rest.  The surrounding area's inhabitants breathe a sigh of relief.  The village elders will now be able to live a comfortable life again on the toil and sweat of their people.  Oh, joy!

You come to a massive iron gate.  It is three feet thick and reinforced with hammered iron banding.  You have never encountered such an impenetrable gate.  Using the normal methods of breaking and entering, you are unable to budge it open.
While you are traversing some rough terrain, large boulders begin to tumble down from above.  You look up and see giants hurling the boulders like pebbles.
Fully three dozen giants are perched atop the tall ridge overlooking the valley.  The ridge is very narrow and any one of them could easily fall to a quick death.

Unfortunately, their height advantage makes their missiles incredibly effective. Yours fall far short of their mark.  Your only choice may be to try and rush past them in a mad attempt to gain access to the fortress beyond - a risky option at best.

The Horn of Annoyance blares its obnoxious sound once again.  Perilously perched on outcroppings, the giants grab their heads in total dismay. Most lose their balance and fall to a quick demise.  Their bodies are gruesomely smashed on the rocks below.
The few giants who are left try desperately to maintain their footing.  You make an easy dash for the fortress.  The gods of protection have smiled upon you with favor.

Your clever use of magic has been effective for the most part.  Many giants are fooled.  A few comprehend what is transpiring and try to counteract.  Some boulders still find their mark, but you are past the danger before long.

Because enemies aren't expected to penetrate this deep into their territory,  entrance to the fortress is relatively easy. It's hard to believe that you have gotten beyond the great mountains and are now in the front line fortress of the giant stronghold.
You discover a storage room.  It is mostly empty.  From its appearance, you presume that it is not frequently used.  It should be safe to rest here.

You enter one of the main sections on the ground floor of this monstrous-sized keep.  A few unimportant documents scattered about reveal that this is the fortress Martech.  Luckily, there are no guards in the entry chamber, but you hear...
deep voices.  Growls come from several directions at once.
You see hill giants shuffling your way.  You could easily hide.  Would you rather attack them?
This door is unlocked.  You open it and look down a long, dark hallway.  The smell of feces is pervasive.  The screams of creatures in pain haunt the dismal passage.

You peer through iron bars.  A large room with many doors comes to view.  A giant supervises several trolls who are torturing a large gnath.  Another gnath is tied face down to a bench.  Its bloody back is covered with whip marks.
You gather that the gnaths are being punished.  During their last raid, they failed to totally destroy a human village, and many of the villagers escaped unharmed.  What do you wish to do?
You burst through the door and quickly kill all the gnaths.  Since they were already tied up, it was easy to slit their throats.
The wounded gnaths do not even stop to give thanks.  They quickly leave through the doorway you came in.
A large gnath is inside this cell.  Do you wish to release him?

He stands, brushes moldy straw from his body, and speaks to you in common, "I have seen what you did for my brothers.  Take this key.  The guards weren't aware that I had stolen it.  It opens a cellar door where a great treasure is guarded."
I must go now and help my tribe rebel against the giants.  We are surely doomed if we remain under their influence.
Unarmed, he is not looking for a fight.  He slips around you and bolts for the door.
Unsuccessful at moving silently.  A troll hears your movements and points you out.
Having defeated the guards, do you want to free the gnaths or kill them?
Do you want to make a break for the fortress or do you choose to retreat?

You attempt to get to the fortress by making a mad dash over the rough terrain.  Agile dodging enables you to avoid many of the hurtling boulders heaved your way.  However, enough find their mark to make the flight a costly endeavor.
You come upon an elite unit of minotaur troops.  Do you attack them?
You leave the fortress Martech.

You venture beyond the reaches of the fortress Martech.  You head into the Grim Mountains.  This is the giants' stronghold.  The chances of encountering a friendly traveler will be slim, now that you are on this side of the pass.
Journeying through a rocky pass, you once again emerge on the northeastern side of the grim wall.
The cave dead ends here.  There is a large hole in the floor.  You look down into a spiraling tunnel.  Do you wish to enter?

As you descend, anxiety pumps up your heart rate.  Dampness wraps around you like a cold, living snake.  Rank odors of death and rot assault your nostrils.  The walls are coated with eerily glowing moss.

You notice a strong, distinctive scent and discover an old half-burned torch lying at your feet.  It appears to be radiating magic.  The moldy fungus you were using as a light source suddenly thins and fades away.  You are left in total darkness.

Scrambling in the dark, you make several frustrating attempts to strike up your own torch lights or cast light by magical means.  For some peculiar reason, these methods fail miserably.  Do you wish to try and use the half-burned magical torch you found?
The magical torch lights up easily.  Much to your dismay, you suddenly recognize a distinctive odor emitting from it.  It's a natural gas that is notoriously known for its flammability.

The noxious fumes do not last long.  Luckily, there is enough oxygen in the small cave to support both the torch and your breathing.  You now clearly see that you are standing in a small room.  The only way out is the way you came in.

The wall is covered with strange writings  you have never seen before.  A stone casket lies open.  Peering in, you are able to make out the indentations of a powerful sword impressed into the casket's velvet-lined interior.  The sword is now missing.

Abruptly, the magical writings begin to rearrange themselves before your very eyes.  In seconds, they become legible.  You are informed that the powerful weapon has been deliberately moved in an effort to thwart its falling into evil hands.

You spot an odd-looking dry patch of grass.  It appears strangely out of place.  You scrape away the grass and uncover a heavy iron door embedded in the ground.  Do you wish to open this unusual door?

Pulling vigorously, you manage to crack the seal and gaze down into an inner recess.  A small bundle wrapped within a moldy, silken shroud lies within a small, oblong niche.  Hastily peeling away the shroud, you unveil a weapon of magnificent beauty.

Runes describing historical, glorious battles are inscribed along the length of its metallic blade.  You decipher the runes on the pommel and interpret their meaning to be: "SALVATION".  It is a mighty weapon.

The magical writings disclose how evil forces discovered an ancient text revealing the hidden resting place of this mighty weapon.  They sought to steal it for their own evil purposes.  However, good forces were able to move it to its present safe haven.

Many places were considered for Giant Slayer's new resting place.  It was finally decided that a remote place would be safest.  You have been carefully watched and judged.  This information has been revealed to you because of your inner goodness.

In future times of need, seek out the Giant Slayer 21 leagues to the east.  Turn and continue traveling north for 14 additional leagues.  There you will find an iron door concealed by nature.  Within its confines, you shall find salvation.
The writings slowly revert back to their former illegible state.

A sign over the door reads, "Honest Buttafooco's Equipment, Storage and Novelty Shop."  This looks like a good place to store your excess baggage for the reasonable fee of 100 gold pieces.  Do you pay the fee to enter?
"Those two!  Mother of Mesaba!  Yeah, I know dem.  Dey two friends o' yours?  Dey owe me a good deal o' coin.  If you find dem, you let me know.  I'd be right appreciative.

"Last time I got wind o' dem, dey was headed to one o' the town wells to get a sip o' drink.  Said dey had a big mission and needed clear heads.  Bah!  De two o' dem couldn't be trusted to tie der own shoes.  I told dem, dey would have better...
luck finishin' der big secret mission if dey dove in the lake.  See, I was thinkin' a bit o' water might help dem sober up a bit. I seen dey needed a bit o' soberin' real bad."

The barkeeper babbles on about his cousin Frit attempting to hook up with some travelers.  Two local barflies start a scuffle, ripping a sconce right out of the wall.  Shouting epithets, the barkeeper abruptly stomps off to crack some heads together.

To your amazement, the chest and its immediate surroundings show no signs of being scorched by the blast.  A great battle-axe lies within the chest.  It shines with an incredible aura.  This is a sure sign that the weapon possesses strong, magical powers.

Lord Oswald listens to your progress concerning your quest in search of the Axe of Ashblet.  After a brief period, he ends your account with a wave of his hand, "My friends, it is obvious more work lies ahead of you.  I will detain you no longer."

"Well done, my friends! Well done, indeed!  This bodes well for our future triumph in battle.  Now that we've obtained the Axe of Ashblet, the dwarves will align with us against the giants.  Such an alignment is vital to our success in the upcoming war.

You are honorable and noble to relinquish such a fine weapon.  Believe me, when I say that the cause is a worthy one.  I am deeply grateful and humbly offer you this fine weapon in exchange.  It's been a cherished family heirloom for numerous generations.

Lord Oswald talks with you briefly.  However, you sense that he is anxious to send word to the dwarves regarding his  possession of the Axe.  You courteously take your leave, and Lord Oswald turns to more pressing duties.
This roomy cave is tucked away into a remote portion of a huge cave complex.  Although fortunate for most underground dwellers, this proves to be unfortunate for you!

Piercing cries ring out.  Huge creatures simultaneously descend from the cavernous ceiling.  Their reptilian bodies flash about like lightning.  You are unwillingly caught up in a battle of mammoth proportions.

This small cave leads into an endless series of underground caverns.  The ceiling  is extremely high.  Bats couldn't fly any more freely than if they lived under open sky.  Many animals live and die here without ever leaving these underground chambers.
Well, it had to happen.  This is where you have to endure the registration process.  Enter the registration name as it appears on the form you received from us in return for your registration fee.

A small boat lies damaged and abandoned on the shore.  You inspect the boat and the ground nearby more closely.  Evidence suggests that a violent struggle has occurred.  A bloody trail leads off in a northeasterly direction.

You are approaching a small shack.  From a distance, you hear the tortured screams of a woman.  Another woman cackles loudly and hideously.  Malicious, she enjoys inflicting pain and torturing her victim.  Chills run up your spine.  Do you approach?

You are about to peek into the shack's crude window.  Suddenly, you are assaulted with a stream of rocks.  A large group of ogres has spotted your approach and is running in your direction.  They bellow a warning to the cruel torturer inside.

You spin around to confront the ogres' onslaught.  The female torturer bursts forth from the shack.  She points her hand in the direction of the ogres and barks a single word.  They quickly halt and stare at her in fear.

She scrutinizes you carefully.  Her eyes seem to bore right through you.  You have the strange feeling that she is aware of your innermost secrets.  Her voice is slow and raspy, "You do not belong here.  I don't deal with the likes of you.  Leave now...
or you shall forever curse yourself for coming here."  Do you decide to call her bluff and attack?

She responds immediately with a wave of her hand and casts a spell.  A streaking, blue magical flame darts in your direction.  To your wondrous surprise, the flame flies over your heads and strikes the group of ogres.

You say a quick prayer thanking the gods for her poor aim.  However, you soon realize that you were never the target.  The ogres shriek painful screams as they transform into beasts even more hideous.  You are quickly engaged in deadly battle.

A formidable foe.  However, she shall never trouble you again.  You burst into the shack to free the tortured prisoner and are shocked at the scene before you.  Strapped to a crude workbench, this woman had probably once been considered quite normal.

Now she has been mutated from the waist upwards into a monstrous marine-like creature.  Her screams are now muffled as she attempts to voice her pain through gill slits.  Her eyes are covered by thick milky white inner eyelids.
Do you wish to put her out of her misery? OR  Do you wish to set her free?  Her torturer is dead.  Perhaps the magic will fade in time, and she will return to normal.

Mercifully, you swiftly slay the poor soul.  You search the shack and find the remains of several others.  Many of them suffered through various stages of transformation before dying horrible deaths.  Their torturer practiced a cruel form of alchemy.

You cut the bonds that are holding captive this degenerate form of nature.  The woman continues to mutate before your very eyes and completely transforms into some strange aquatic leviathan.  It gawks at you with its glassy eyes.

The creature creases its face.  You interpret this as a smile.  The crease widens further.  You get a great view of a mouth full of sharp teeth dripping caustic venom.  It is not a smile, but a sneer!  The mutant launches itself at you in a frenzy.
You search the shack and find the remains of many others in various stages of transformation.  They all died gruesome, agonizing deaths.  Their torturer practiced a cruel form of alchemy.
The mutant's remains pop and sizzle.  They quickly decompose into a pool of goo and greasy smoke.
A small tunnel leads off in a westward direction.
This cave is currently occupied by a band of ogres.  They are not pleased to see you.

This cave is occupied by a large band of ogres.  One stands up and stares at you with eyes the size of keska balls.  He manages a few words in Common, "You no belong here.  Leave, and me forget.  Me too hungry to kill you right now."

Several sheep are being roasted over a spit near the ogres' feet.  Most likely they were stolen from an honest farmer.  Then they probably murdered him to prevent their raid from being reported to the kings' men.  Do you attack these plunderers?
You are not the only ones to show your bravado.  The ogre leader rises to his full height.  Standing fully three feet taller than any ogre you have ever seen, he is a giant even amongst his own kind.
You stumble upon an odd hole in the ground.  The ground has caved in somewhat along the hole's edges.  Do you wish to lower someone down and explore the inside?

Cave insects buzz abnormally loud in an immense underground cavern.  Many are feasting upon the rotting remains of twelve humans and two dwarves.  The humans were probably farmers.  The dwarves are too decomposed to determine sex or trade.

Nearby is a small lake of water.  Bubbles rise to its surface.  You suspect that the pool has an underground source.  You dive in to discover a shallow underground river that emerges on a small island some distance away.
You spot large boulders that sit just below the water's surface in close proximity to one another.  You can use them as a bridge to cross over to other sections of the lake.
You make your way to a small island.
Floundering around in a strange underground cavern's lake can prove to be a dangerous activity.  You are about to learn a hard lesson.
You spot some rocks just below the surface of the water.  Getting off this island will be a snap.

The sounds of combat ring out nearby.  You rush to the scene and see the kings' men fiercely engaged in battle with a patrol of ogres led by a giant.  The kings' men fight valiantly, but they are being overpowered.  You jump into the fray!
You tend to the wounded.  Many have died, any many more are in great agony.  Local clerics arrive and bless you for your help in driving off the invaders.

The village temple.  It serves many denominations.  The small village can only financially support one house of worship, and it must serve the beliefs of many.   Local acolytes tend to your ailments and those of others.

A small, dismal shop.  The portly shop owner explains, "It's been difficult to obtain supplies since the raids began.  Most people with good coin have already fled to the city.  Conditions are very hard on the rest of us."

A seedy-looking fellow intercepts you outside the shop's entrance.  "Friends, this is your lucky day!  You've got money to spend, and I just got back from the western lands.  I could sell you some valuable objects at a good price."  Interested?

You have come to the only way in or out of Black Earth village.  A few of the king's men stand at the gateway keeping a wary lookout.  Many of the village huts stand empty.  Most villagers have already fled to the city.

A harried villager rushes by.  You accost him and try to pump him for news. "I'm leavin' soon as I can.  My kinfolk are packin' right now and headin' for the city.  Them gnaths to the south are too close for comfort.  I've got my wee ones to think of."

Almost everyone appears possessed by feelings of frantic fear.  Gnaths have constructed a stronghold just south of the village.  Many of the outlying farms have been raided already.  It won't be much  longer before they attack...
Most people are hoping to be long gone before the gnaths attack the village.  Although the king's men patrol the walls, they aren't numerous enough to ease the  locals' fear.

Bored and dissatisfied, you wander about aimlessly.  The village offers little for entertainment.  Suddenly, there is a massive rumbling to the south.  You see a huge section of the mountain crumble inward.  Gnaths pour from the mountain.  It's a raid!

The entire town erupts in panic.  You and the small group of king's men guarding the village rush to the area and attempt to throw back the attackers.  A skirmish line forms.  The villagers are given little time to escape with their lives.

Gnaths continue to pour out of the mountain passage.  Many initial shock troops have fallen as a result of your superior combat skills.  The gnath ranks are now diluted with younger warriors, but they are still an effective fighting force.

The carnage continues.  The death toll mounts.  You try to catch your breath.  A third squad of gnaths emerges from the mountain and presses the attack.  They have been reduced to young warriors with only a few veterans.  Your side fares no better.
An incredible battle!  You send a runner to the king to inform him of your great victory.

It's now apparent why the gnaths didn't attack earlier.  The creation of this tunnel was an immense undertaking, requiring  months of time and considerable effort.  No longer a secret, it now offers a way of gaining entry into the gnaths' stronghold.

You turn a corner in the tunnel and are nearly bowled over by another squad of gnaths.  They were attempting to pull a large wagon of lumber towards the village.  The cramped conditions make the ensuing struggle for power an arduous task.

You study the wagon's lumber and tools,   and conclude that the gnaths' plans were  to gain village control, build catapults and siege engines.  You have foiled their intentions and have probably saved many lives.

You dive into the water but are unable to find the spring's source.  You swim a considerable distance and finally spot light from above.  You pull yourself up through a hole similar to the one you encountered earlier.  The island also seems familiar.
You have accidentally been caught up in the throes of a fierce battle.  A large group of giant ants is attacking a smaller group of beetles.

A heavy iron door blocks your path.  The thick door has been crafted out of hammered iron.  From the other side of the door, you can faintly hear gruff voices.  You think they are speaking the dwarven tongue.  Do you knock?

There is a dreadful silence followed by curses of startled alarm.  You hear the loud clash and din of armor as it is hastily retrieved and put on.  A voice on the other side calls to you in a deep booming voice,  "Who ye be?"
"We do not know this king of which you speak.  He wields no power here! Clan Forgefire rules this domain! Begone, or we shall slay you all!"
"We refuse to take the risk of allowing giant ants access to our domain!  The Clan is not interested in your petty problems."

The dwarves on the other side begin to mumble.  Curious, they decide to check if you are still out there.  A small chute above the iron door pops open.  Large rocks rain down.  Painful shouts and enraged threats reveal that you haven't left.

Your foul debasements provoke the  dwarves' wrath.  "Why, we'll send you to an early grave and snap your puny little necks with our bare hands!"  You hear a large metal bar being slid aside.  The heavy door opens with an earsplitting screech.
You stand face-to-face with a group of surly dwarves.  You can try to soothe their feelings or engage in combat.  Do you try to smooth things over?

"As always, you wanderers are real brave until it comes time for battle.  Then you're all yellow.  Lucky for you, I'm in a forgiving mood.  Come in.  We can't have a bunch of weaklings crying outside our door all day."

You come upon a small shack covered with  a unique variety of grass.  A wall of stalagmites surrounds the shack.  Several tracks bestrew the ground around the fence's wall.  You can make out more tracks within the wall's confines.
A faint smell of tobacco drifts outward from the hut.  Do you approach the hut silently?  OR  Do you call out a hail for its inhabitant(s) to come out?
You are attacked by a platoon of dwarven warriors.

This is the dwelling of the clan council.  It is a stout building built of granite boulders.  They are fit together with such skill, they do not even require mortar.   You step inside and are greeted by the clan chief and his advisors.

You are addressed by the clan chief, Breagor Forgefire. "Split Beard tells me you threatened to beat him, if he didn't let you in.  Haaah!  He could use a good beating!  I would do it myself, but I thought it more fitting to have him...

guard the east entrance.  One duty every dwarf hates is guard duty.  Split Beard drank a whole keg of my best ale.  I set him to guardin' the east entrance 'cause nothin' has happened there in over four years.  Now, out of the darkness a strange...

lot shows up and expects entrance.  So be it, I say.  This clan has lived in deliberate isolation for over 250 years as we tried to heal from the pain and suffering caused by the horrid giant wars.  We cannot hide  forever.  We must overcome our fears.

Two hill dwarves were here a couple of moons ago.  They informed us that a great war, perhaps deadlier than the first, was about to start.  I promised Lord Oswald and the king that I would help them crush the giants, if they fulfilled my one request.

They would have to return the Axe of Ashblet to us.  My life's desire has been to find the Axe and pledge my unremitting loyalty to Reorx himself.  However, I am unable to quest for the Axe.  My vow to watch over my clan cannot be broken.
Lord Oswald has promised that he will make every effort to return the Axe.  Until I receive the Axe, I will have nothing to do with this impending war.

Your discovery of the Axe of Ashblet causes the king to weep for joy.  He cradles the Axe in his arms like a mother  holds a newborn babe.  The entire village erupts in cheers.  The village council crowds around to hear your story of its recovery.

Music and several skins of spiced wine and dwarven ale enliven many hours of joyful feasting.  The chief finally calls an end to the celebration.  He stands in the village center and speaks, "Clan! Clan! Gather round.  We dwarves love our drink...

but our celebration must be a short one.  The time has come.  I must pledge my loyalty to Reorx, and we must all pledge our allegiance to Lord Oswald and his king.  They have fulfilled their part of the agreement...

We dwarves shall live up to ours.  In two Sespian days, we shall set out for Lord Oswald's stronghold and pledge our axes to his service.  Enjoy a few more hours of celebration.  The time of marching draws near."

You are escorted to private quarters for a meeting with the chief.  "My friends, what you have done for us has value without measure.  I can never fully repay you, but I shall do all I can.  I have gathered together the finest armor...

ever to be forged within Clan Fireforge.   Please accept it as my gift for a debt that can never be fully repaid."  Pulling off a tarp, he reveals a vast, shining display of superior armor.  "If you like, you may rest here indefinitely.  However, I..."

must prepare to lead the clan's journey to the surface.  Our kin has not set foot there in a long time.  I greatly fear many will never see this home again.  May Reorx always watch and guide you."  Overcome by emotion, he turns and walks away.
The chief invites you to stay as long as you like.  Regrettably, his duties shall keep him far too busy to play host.  He hopes that you find your stay comfortable.
An old dwarf pops his head through a tiny window.  "Hullo!  Come 'round back.  Take the east path.  The north path is too dangerous."  Do you take the north or east path?

The old dwarf hears all of his traps being set off.  He yells to you from a different window, "Hey!  You deaf or something?  I told you to go the other way!  You've set off every trap I had.  I'll have to go back and reset them all later.  Come on in."

You enter the old shack.  The old dwarf has settled into a rickety-looking rocking chair.  He is fast asleep.  Your entrance startles him awake.  "Who?  Now, you young ones run along and play...  Wait!  You're not...   Visitors!  Welcome!"  He smiles.
"Sit down and rest a spell."  You set down your load.  Before you even begin to relax, the old dwarf begins to fall asleep again.  What do you do?
This is not just another cave entrance.  It's the entrance to a giant ant colony.  You're in big trouble!
More giant ants boil up from below to resume the assault.

Another group of ants burst out from the tunnels below.  There could be thousands of these mindless creatures.  Eventually, your fatigue will overcome you, and you  will be overthrown.  It would be wise to leave these ants alone.
You have stumbled on a bunch of traps. They were originally set to capture giant ants.  However, you have become the unlucky victim.
You peer through a window.  An old dwarf sits sleeping in a dilapidated rocking chair.  You step inside.

"You young pups aren't too bright. Why,  those traps keep the ants in and me out.  Or they keep me in and the ants out. I forget which. Well, it keeps us apart. That much I know. Yes, it keeps the ants away." He smiles, satisfied with his explanation.

Reaching under his chair, the dwarf pulls out an atomizer.  He quickly sprays you with a sweet-smelling perfume.  You know that insects are attracted to sweet-smelling objects.  Uneasy, you cannot account for the dwarf's outrageous behavior.
You would bid the dwarf good-bye, but he is already asleep.
This cave is occupied by huge, foul creatures that look vaguely familiar.  You abruptly recall that long ago you read about them in an ancient tome.  They are larva.  Do you wish to attack them?

You begin to sift through an immense pile of bones.  Only a few belonged to humanoids.  Most of the debris appears worthless.  However, your eyes are abruptly drawn to an object.  It's glowing with a magical radiance.

The Mush-Men are tending their mushroom fields and are exterminating all pests in this area.  Unwittingly, you have been caught in the midst of this major extermination campaign.  They consider you field pests and plan to eliminate you shortly.
This grove of cave mushrooms is tended by a colony of Mush-Men.  They view you as common garden pests and attempt to exterminate you.
You enter a large cavern.  The rocky floor has been planted with copious, orderly rows of giant mushrooms.
A water spring bubbles up from the cavern depths to provide water for the mushroom fields.

You enter a large interconnected network of small caves.  Kegs of freshwater and rations are in abundance.  These caves must be the dwarves' main storage facilities.  You replenish your supply of freshwater and rations.

This cave opens up into a large cavern.  Its floor is rough and uneven.  The dwarves have not used this area for storage or for anything else.  Perhaps they considered the area too bothersome to work with because of the floor's condition.
There is a good reason why the dwarves never pushed their borders north.  It would require a tremendous effort to evict the current tenant from this cave.
You are confronted by one of the most ferocious creatures you have ever seen.
The bones of diverse creatures lie strewn about the entrance to this large cave.  Similar piles of bones lie scattered throughout the cave.  A very powerful creature must dwell here.

You chance upon the creature's nest and discover a large egg.  Hopefully, the slain creature does not have a protective mate lurking somewhere nearby.  You could be in grave danger.  Do you swipe the egg?
You encounter a group of krise.  Your  party could easily overpower them in combat.  They are keenly aware of this and attempt to reason with you.

"Once we lived in the caves south of here and had a great tribe.  Years ago, the dwarves defeated us and forced us to retreat to this cave.  Unable to escape, we have spent our lives trying to capture enough food to keep the great beast fed...

When we failed, the beast fed on us.  Over the years our tribe has slowly dwindled.  Only a few of us remain.  Now the beast is about to spawn a youngling.  Our tribe will soon meet its demise in an effort to quench this newborn creature's hunger.
Do you attack the krise?  OR  Do you show pity and let them go?
