Though they are weak, they swarm over you in vast numbers.  You could easily  sweep them away, but you've been caught unprepared.  You frantically try to set up skirmish lines.  They manage to get in a  few strikes at some of your slower party members.

It appears as if this section of the cavern has been used very rarely.  You discover a hidden passage.  The entrance has been cleverly disguised to fit into the rock wall.  Somehow, you accidentally triggered it open.  It is of dwarven make.
A woman sits crying inside a nicely kept hut.  You investigate to see if she is in danger.  She tells you a sad tale, "My name is Sasha.  My entire family has been cast out by the clan.

Three years ago my grandpap became sick with a withering disease.  Soon my entire family had caught the sickness except for me.  The elders held a clan meeting.  They ruled that my family be banished forever to prevent the sickness from spreading.

On the day they were ordered to be driven out of the clan, my family could not be found.   Ashamed and embarrassed at being banished by their own kin, they had secretly fled the night before.  I have grieved their loss ever since.

The village cleric was granted a glorious vision only a few days ago. The gods told him how to cure the disease. Sadly, I cannot even hope to cure my family and enable their return. I have no idea where they are. Also, the portent speaks in riddles:

"Only new life can stave off the withering death.  Sup on the life force of thy mightiest foe before thy foe's own life begins."  So far, the meaning behind these words has remained a puzzling mystery.  She weeps, and you leave her alone to mourn.
You enter a cave of substantial size.   A small shack stands alone.  Some forlorn grave plots are off to its right.   The smell of rot and diseased flesh dwells heavily in the air.

A male dwarf is sleeping inside the hut.  His face is covered with foul-looking lesions.  He awakens in alarm. "Who are you?  What are you doing here?" You explain your intentions.  He believes that you mean him no harm and tells you his story.

I was once a proud and respected member of Clan Forgefire. My family was banished from the clan when we became infected by this cruel disease. The entire family was wiped out. The only exception was my granddaughter. We left her behind with the clan.

My family never wanted to be separated from their kin, but we could not risk the danger of the disease spreading.  We have hidden in this cave for three years.  One by one, I have watched them all die of the withering disease.

My time is short.  My only regret is that there will be no one left to bury me next to my beloved family.  Alas, if there only was a cure for this foul disease.  The village cleric tried every healing power.  Nothing helped.
The old dwarf is overcome by a coughing fit.   Tired and exhausted, he passes out on his sickbed.

You feed the Beast Lizard Egg to the ailing dwarf.  The life force that was originally destined to bear forth a monstrosity is now absorbed by the dwarf's body.  His lesions heal in a matter of seconds, and he becomes remarkably strong and healthy.

"I cannot believe my own eyes.  I am as healthy as I was three years ago before the disease infected me.  Thank you, my friends.  You do not know what this means to me.  I only wish the cure had come earlier.  I could have saved my family.

His face brightens, "I can still look forward to reuniting with my granddaughter.  For that, you have my eternal thanks. I wish I could pay you with material riches, but I am not wealthy."  He excitedly gathers his things together for his journey.
You find a narrow shaft in the back of this cave.  It's a tight fit, but you can squeeze through.
You begin to make your escape, distancing yourself from the nest.  Suddenly, the beast lizard's mate shows up.  It had heard the lizard's final death cry and has now arrived to investigate.
As the great beast collapses, it emits a hideous death cry.  The deafening noise rings off the cave walls like a series of charalon bells.
A stiff breeze flows outward from a small tunnel.  Rocks hide the tunnel's entrance from your direct view.  You peer inside the tunnel, but it goes back farther than you can see.
This small cavern is seething with giant spiders.
Your entry into the cave causes quite a stir.  The insects band together to defend their lair.  They pour down the tunnel after you.  Battle ensues.
This opening is an entry point to a giant ant colony.  The colony is of immense proportions.  Warrior ants guard the colony's entrance.  Some worker ants serve as reinforcements to these guards.
The queen ant is in the area.  If you press your attack you may be able to reach her and kill her.  Do you press your attack in hopes of killing the queen?
You drive towards the queen.  She is attended by several worker ants.  Before you can reach her, you are intercepted by a group that rushes to her defense.
Nothing stands between you and the queen.  You dive in to make the kill.  Her death will lead to the collapse of the colony.
With the queen dead, the colony has no future.  Seconds after her death, the ants  begin to disintegrate into a state of confused disorganization.  They lose all interest in you.
You are no longer being harassed by ants  and can continue your explorations with ease.

You discover that the north wall is an illusion.  A small iron box has been hidden behind the false wall.  Several dated, now unimportant papers have been stored in the box.  You lift the papers out and uncover an interesting item.
These stairs lead downwards.  The air grows cold and damp as you descend.
You ascend the stairs to the first floor.
You fall victim to a poisonous needle.  You are lucky.  Due to age, the poison has lost most of its potency.
Success!
Failure.
This door is locked.
You have triggered a trap.

You find a small opening chiseled into the mountain side.  At one time, the opening had successfully been concealed by shrubbery.  However, the recent spell of hot, sunny days has shriveled it up considerably.  The opening is now clearly exposed.
You come upon a group of ghouls.  You feel tense and uneasy.  Several have a strange look about them.  They look like ghouls, yet are different somehow.  Do you wish to attack them?
You stumble upon the only place in the entire cavern that is not littered with the bones of the dead.  For one reason or another, the undead appear unwilling to cross this river.

The ungodly stench of this place makes you feel ill.  Moans and wails echo throughout the caverns.  Gnawed bones and half-eaten corpses litter the floor.  Judging by the numerous footprints,  many of the undead have passed through here.

You step into a very crowded tavern.  The smell of meat, cheese and breads of all types fill the air.  One would never guess that the land was on the brink of war.  You worry that massive death and destruction will be suffered unless great changes occur.

You are crowded by peoples of all the civilized races.  You suspect that you're not the only adventurer here.  Many in the crowd appear powerful, short-tempered, or dangerous.  It would be wise to stay clear of many of these characters.

You sit at an empty table.  A strong hand clamps down and squeezes the shoulder of one of your party members in a vise-like grip.  A very large orc dressed in exquisite plate armor demands that you remove yourself from his seat.  Do you remain seated?
His voice booms throughout the tavern as he barks out several words in an unrecognizable language.  Several warriors and sinister-looking spell casters quickly form a tight circle around you.

A powerful mage has been sitting on a stool behind the bar. Before you can react, he stands. His commanding presence invokes utter stillness. "Refrain from this folly.  Fight your battles elsewhere. Proponents of rash actions will not be tolerated here."

The mage stands fifty feet away. A shimmering gem magically appears in his hand. With a deft flick, the gem shoots in your direction and lands on your table. There is a blinding flash. When the spots clear from your eyes, you and your provokers...
are teleported some distance away from the tavern.  Your opponents recover their senses before you do.  They attempt to take advantage of your present state of confusion.

These mighty opponents should not have chosen to become your foes.  Obsessed by their need for domination and control, they were deliberately cruel and abusive towards others.  Their foolhardiness has finally made them pay for their wicked ways.

You excitedly begin to sort through your opponents' belongings.  They possessed many items of great worth.   Unfortunately, before you can pocket the equipment and coins, you are teleported back to the tavern.

Annoyed, you find yourself sitting back at your table.  The mage who teleported you eyes you severely. "You have no need of their equipment.  It will serve to repay me for your disturbance of the peace.  I suggest you enjoy a fine meal and move on."

Your way is barred by a man of colossal stature.  You envision him eating his meals raw, tearing meat chunks with bare hands.  Amazingly, he enunciates his words with the diction of a pre-eminent scholar. "Pardon me. This club is for members only."

He leans close and lowers his voice confidentially.  "We allow only the finest clientele.  However, if you are willing to donate a sum of 30 gems, I'm sure they would allow you to enter for a trial membership."  Do you pay this outrageous fee?
"Very well.  It's your decision."  Although he doesn't lay a hand on you, his penetrating gaze and compelling manner propels you unrelentingly back into the street.
"Very good.  You're welcome to look around."  With a polite, quirky nod of the head, he allows you to enter.

An attractive servant provides you with directions to the sanitary facilities.  One single room is being used by all, and it is currently locked.  You originally think that someone must be using it.  After waiting several minutes, you begin to wonder.

The last occupant either left it locked or is simply refusing anyone entry.  There is no response to your repeated knocks.  You angrily pick the lock and step inside to investigate.  Horrified, you discover the ghastly remains of a well-dressed woman.

Dressed in fine black velvet, her frail body lies in a crumpled, forlorn heap on the floor.  The killer has used her blood to paint the walls with strange demonic symbols.  You hear a small noise coming from a closet.
Do you investigate the noise?  OR  Do you summon aid?

Several guards dressed in regal armor arrive. They hastily hustle you out of the room. You are warned not to discuss this with anyone. As you're leaving, you overhear one guard say, "Cavela better do something soon. That makes three in the last month."
Before you pass out of earshot, you overhear the guards voice the names of the suspected killers.  They are "Rewop" and "Mood".  The first name sounds strangely familiar.

As soon as you open the closet, a blinding blur of nails and teeth flashes past you and bolts for the door.  You believe that the raving creature is a Cacodeamon - a vicious beast often summoned from the nether plains to perform a service.

These creatures are ruthless killers, skilled at evading capture.  It quickly outmaneuvers you, darts through an open window, and disappears into the shadows of nearby structures.  In the process, your point companion acquires a slight scratch.
Your friend's eyes become glassy and unfocused.  Alarmed, you reach out and touch flesh that feels cold and stiff.  In a matter of seconds, your companion has completely turned to stone.

You attempt to ingratiate yourself through small talk but begin to grow bored.  The conversation is much too superficial to hold your interest.  A suspicious-looking gentleman leaves in a sudden hurry.  Do you attempt to follow?

You soon lose his trail and are unable to pick it up again.  Apprehensive, you realize that you have strayed into a very seedy-looking portion of town.  Before you can return to a safer area, you are beset by thieves.
The thieves have an unusually large number of torches among their possessions.  Many have been partially used and are emitting a pungent aroma.  You suspect that they've been used quite recently.

You cautiously begin to case the joint.  A group of armored men brings your  investigations to an abrupt conclusion.  "Many odd events have taken place of late.  Your strange behavior just now suggests that you may know something."

They roughly seize you for questioning.  After several exhausting sessions, they decide that you did not play a part in any of the recent crimes. Unwilling to take  chances, they escort you out of town and instruct you not to return under pain of death.
You are intercepted by some of Lord Jericho's hired henchmen.  They bar your path and order to you stay clear of the city.  Do you attempt to use force to stay?
You spot a patrol of Lord Jerico's men.  Do you wish to attack them?

"What do you want, strangers?  I'm a busy man and have much to do."  You attempt to gain his ear.  He gazes off in an entirely different direction. "Yes, yes. I'm listening."  Although he insists that he's listening, he pays you no attention at all.
An impressive group of warriors hails you.  They approach you in an unthreatening manner.  Do you attack them?

"Hail, good people. I'm Captain Kespen of Lord Jerico's contingent of storm troopers. This city is under his control. No strangers are allowed at this time. I am merely here to warn you. Those that attempt to circumvent this law will be severely punished.

"Wait! There may be something you can do for me. I am Baron Brigadoon, and I need to hire an assassin to have someone killed.  If you think you are capable of handling such a task, I would reward you MOST generously."  Do you accept?

"Good! This map shows the location of a small hut. There you will find a frail man. Don't believe the rumors about him dabbling in the black arts.  He's an old dotard with little real power. I'd do it myself, but he has powerful friends.
"When the job is complete, you can find me waiting here.  You will be rewarded with a fitting gift once you have successfully carried out your mission."

Just as described, you find the frail old man inside his hut.  You guess that he must be at least ninety years old.  He is babbling incoherently to himself.  At the same time, he is intently bending over a table covered with several ancient books.
Do you fulfill your contract and immediately slay the man?  OR   Do you inform him of the situation and give him a chance to make a better counteroffer?

You burst in on the man and quickly slit his throat.  The life drains quickly from his body.  He looks at you as if to say something, but he cannot speak.  His vocal cords have been cut clean through.

As you approach the club the baron suddenly pokes his head out a window.  He points to you and screams, "There they are! Those are the ones who slew Lord Jerico.  Don't let them escape!"  Guards rush you from all sides.
A large force of armored men approach from the east.  They are accompanied by several spell casters.  You could never defeat such a considerable force.  You attempt to flee.
You maintain a low profile and successfully avert contact with several other patrols.  You reach the town's perimeter without further conflict.
The books littering the table are written in a language that you are unfamiliar with.  Pictures of strange demonic symbols cover their pages.  One symbol distinctly stands out from the others.

The old man slowly shuffles to the door. He answers in a tremulous voice, "Yes, what do you want? I am very busy!" He eyes you warily.  His gaze nervously darts to and fro checking to see if others lurk nearby.  You tell him about the man in the club.

If the old man can grant you a better counteroffer, you will let him live.  Suddenly his feebleness is no longer there.  Wasn't he much shorter a minute ago?  He glares down at you in fierce rage.  The air erupts into flames.  The shack is engulfed.

When the smoke clears, the old man is gone.  You face a huge demonic beast in his place.  Hordes of smaller, deadly replicas of this creature formulate from the fiery ashes.  There is a deep rumbling.  The glowering beast begins to speak.

"Puny mortals! You thought you could cross Visdentil!  Hear my counteroffer. Return to Baron Brigadoon at once and slay him. Refusal will earn you eons of torment and suffering at the hands of my minions." Do you instead choose to fight this menace?

The beast scornfully sneers at your display of force.  You close ranks with the towering creature and his underlings.  With effort, you try to mask your sinking feelings.  This could be one of the worst decisions you ever made.

The area has been totally devastated by the intense battle.  During the struggle, everything of value was either destroyed or is now forever buried beneath the rubble.  A huge contingent of armored men are approaching.
They haven't noticed your presence yet.  You consider it prudent to slip away before they can connect you with this devastation.

You have inadvertently stumbled into a large open hut.  Everywhere you look, numerous butchered horses are turning on spits.  Their bodies slowly simmer over smoldering yabba tree logs.  You find the sight shocking and offensive.
The gate has been magically sealed and  protected to ward against such a spell.
Your clever use of magic grants you passage through the gate.

You arrive at an odd clearing in the middle of the dense woods.  A long, narrow tunnel has been dug down into the earth.  There is room enough to walk through it if you travel single file.  Do you enter the tunnel?
You travel in utter darkness.  The tunnel stretches endlessly.  With relief, you finally come to its end.  You have come back to the surface.
A small giant patrol guards the mountain pass.
The passage comes to a dead end.
This door stands ajar.  It was originally designed to be sturdy and formidable.  Now it has been damaged beyond repair.
A pit opens up beneath your feet.  Members of your party possessing low dexterity are unable to prevent themselves from falling into the pit.
You are in an old storage room.  Nothing of importance is being store here.  The room is empty for the most part and exceedingly dusty.  It may be safe to rest here for awhile.
These stairs lead upwards.
You are in a large room filled with huge cots and large wooden footlockers.  This is the stronghold's barracks.  Unfortunately, some returning troops have discovered your location.

You find the floor captain's footlocker.  It's the only one with a lock.  So far none of the other footlockers have revealed anything of value.  You pry the rusty lock off.  The locker contains a treasure trove of items that must be worth a tidy fortune.

This large room was secretly hidden by the  craftsmen who originally built the fortress.  Once shut, there is no way to open the door from the inside.  Luckily, you were observant enough to notice this before you let the door close.

You immediately prop the door open with some gear.  The last party that ingeniously discovered this place was trapped here forever.   The skeletons of three furfoots sit desolately in a corner.  They were probably an unlucky group of thieves.
You find a few gold pieces, two nice gems, and a ring that glows with a magical luster.
You see several young hill giants playing with crude bone toys in the corner.  Though they are very young, they could give away your location.  You put them to the knife.
A small armory full of giant-size weapons.  They are crudely made.  Their tremendous weight and size also renders them rather worthless to someone of your small stature.

From the far corner of the room, a flicker of light catches your eye.  Several pole arms have been heaped into a large pile.  You maneuver the pole arms aside to reveal a weapon that could be potentially useful.

You cringe at the sight of a pitifully weak trollac chained to the wall.  It's open wounds have become infected.  Brutal torture has reduced this once muscular brute to a quivering mound of flesh.  You show mercy.
This cell is empty.

A giant rat is devouring the corpse of a gnaths.  The beast has engorged itself to such a hideous degree, it can no longer fit through the hole that it entered.  You chop the vermin into small pieces.

This cell appears empty.  You turn to leave.  Suddenly, a group of monsters pounce down from the ceiling rafters and attack you.  They have been aware of your explorations and had planned this ambush in order to escape their prison.
A haggard-looking dwarf sits chained against the wall.  Near death, he is beyond any healing, even magical.  You kneel down at his side to offer him comfort.  He passes away in your arms.

The old dwarf springs back to life.  Although weak, he is capable of walking.  He grasps your hand gratefully for bringing him back from the brink. "My friends, I have something very important to tell you. You must continue my quest, for I cannot."

"I have knowledge of an ancient relic. Possession of this relic is considered vital if we are to ensure the preservation of the free nations.  I do not know it's exact powers.  I only know that it's essential to our cause.  The relic is the Anvil of Pain.

"I have heard rumors that the Anvil has been kept by a clan of dwarves.  My friends, you must seek out the Anvil.  You are hardy and have a better chance of succeeding than I.  The future of the free nations now rests on your shoulders."
"More importantly, you must discover the Anvil's secret.  Our paths part here.  The strength I have left will hopefully be enough to attempt an escape and journey home." He hands you a map.

Numerous giants move purposely about the room efficiently performing various  tasks.  Their industrious activity comes to an abrupt halt, when they are startled by your unwelcome intrusion.  Recovering quickly, they move in for the kill.
On the other side of the door, you can hear several deep, booming voices in a state of excited conversation.  You cannot make out what is being said.  Perhaps, they are arguing.
The boisterous battle attracts the attention of another group of giants working nearby.  They come to investigate all the racket.
Before you can even begin to defend yourselves, you are pelted in the back by a hail of rocks.

A small boy comes up to you and speaks, "Good people, you look ready and eager to seek adventure. The king has paid me five tareks to find those new in town who appear to possess superior qualities. I'm sure that he would like to meet with you."

Trouble is brewing with the giants. If you follow the boy to the castle, the king himself will brief you with more detailed information. The boy claims that he will be paid 2 extra tareks for each adventurer he delivers to the king. Do you follow him?
He leads you to the front gate of the king's castle.  The guards at the gate pay the boy his tareks.  They exhort him to continue searching, then shoo him away.  You are allowed entry to the castle.
The town is being raided.  You are far enough away to easily avoid being drawn into battle.  Do you spring forth to the town's defense and engage in combat?

He places the gold in a sturdy iron box then turns to you. "If necessary, I have the knowledge and expertise to identify any of the items you decide to store here.  Since you're such good customers, I will offer this as an additional free service."
Although the dragons had a sizable treasure cache, most of it consists of gold coins.  You also discover a few precious gems.
Large bones litter the floor of this cavern.  Many bones are cracked.  Their marrow has been sucked dry.  Small scavengers  scuttle busily to and fro picking the remains totally clean.

The bones of many giants lie strewn about the ground.  While you are investigating the area, you are attacked by dragons.  They had been resting near the valley's entrance and were aroused by your movements.
The small stream quickly dries up.  At one time, it must have been much larger.  Erosion has carved a large channel  through the rock.
This portion of the tunnel is riddled with smaller caves that serve as homes for subterranean dwellers.  Upon your approach, the underground dwellers anxiously prepare to defend their homes.

You are confronted by a large contingent of ice giant warriors led by a commander in stunning blue armor.  Several clerics accompany the contingent.  One utters some magical words.  Suddenly, the door slams behind you.
You approach the gates.  Human guards spot you from the walls above.  Excitedly, they beckon in your direction and call to the others within.  "Behold! The rescuers have arrived!"

An earsplitting screech pierces the air.   The unwilling gates are forced open.  Armored men rush out and quickly herd you inside.  Without delay, they heavily ram the gate back into its closed position.  A great crowd gathers around you.  Suddenly...

...a man clothed in full battle gear strides forth from the crowd.  His commanding presence invokes silence among the townspeople.  "Hail, good people! When will the main body of your force arrive?  We had almost given up all hope!"

"I am Captain Samuel Stillwater, the garrison commander.  Steadfast and true, I have managed to uphold this beleaguered town against the giants' onslaughts for months.  The gods bless King Bradwick! Finally, he has sent an army to defend us!"
Do you tell Captain Stillwater who you really are and that no army will be arriving to save the town?  OR   Do you pretend to be an advance scouting party for a massive army?

The captain is unable to mask his depression and sense of futility.  "You best take shelter here with us.  Man the walls!  They will attack soon!"  In his quarters, the captain sadly recounts to you his efforts to defend this forsaken outpost.

The sounds of combat abruptly shatter the peace and quiet.  In the distance, you can see ice giants.  They are launching a hostile attack against a small town.  You are far enough away to avoid being drawn into combat.  Do you rush to the town's defense?

For several months, the giants have  attacked the beleaguered town on a  regular schedule - every ten days.  Today proves to be no exception.  Believing that you are the king's forward guard, the townsfolk expect you to engage in battle.

For months, the giants have been attacking the town on a regular schedule - every ten days.  Today proves to be no exception to the rule.  You don't owe allegiance to the king.  The exhausted townsfolk ask if you will help defend their town.  Do you?

"Good!  We're in desperate need of reinforcements.  I'll pass the news around town.  Goods and food rations are being used sparingly.  The townspeople will be responsible as a whole for seeing that your needs are met."

The town shop.  Because of the town's limited physical strength, many have taken up studies in the arcane powers. People are hoping that the giants can  eventually be conquered by magical means.  The town's shop contains many magical items.

The giants constructed a mighty fortress in the pass. It effectively cut us off from the rest of the kingdom. Originally, we attempted to battle our way through. The casualties were immense. They'd obtained better ground and were far too entrenched.

In order to survive, we were forced to retreat within the town walls. We've  barely managed to retain this ground against their repeated onslaughts. During the past months, the local magicians have begun teaching magic to the townsfolk.

Many are now capable of casting arcane spells of destruction. Sadly, their skills are rudimentary. Many die by their own hand.  Alas! What choice have we?  There is no end to the damnable ice giants' attacks. The only reason why we've survived...

is because they attack on a regular schedule - every ten days without change.  This allows us to prepare a strong defense when necessary.  We can't hold out for very much longer.  The people grow more despondent with each passing day.

Your news of the tunnel is welcome, but our older citizens could never survive such a harsh journey. We must destroy the citadel. I can't spare any men to aid you, but if you could gain entry and destroy it from within, many lives could be saved.

I've helplessly stood by as our children watched their parents die in agony. If we fail, their fate lies along the same path. I can't order you to take on such a dangerous mission. You've no obligation to us, and you'll not be mistreated if you refuse.

I've no more time now for idle chatter.  I must attend to my many duties.  Please, make yourselves at home here.  I'm afraid that a town under siege has little to offer in the way of comforts. However, you're welcome to all that we have."  He departs.

You come face-to-face with the distasteful remains of an elderly giant.  Grotesque, immense worms are rapidly devouring the odorous corpse.  The body is nearly half gone, and these slug-like creatures show no signs of slowing.  Do you attack them?
You find a shield that radiates strong magic.  Nothing else is of any value.

High above you in the sky, a sudden thunderous boom makes you jump involuntarily. You look up just in time to see the limp form of a green dragon crashing to the earth. Flames trail from his body.  Red dragons watch as they circle above.

A mighty red dragon lands and carefully examines the dead body.  After some minutes, the dragon calls to its companions. "The staff is not here!  She has dropped it, as we feared. Take flight! We shall search over the ground from whence she came."

The mighty red leaps a full thirty feet into the air.  A gust of wind hits your face as its powerful wings suddenly flare outward.  Its ascent is rapid. The group banks east and quickly disappears from sight. Do you investigate the green dragon's corpse?

You search the area and are unable to find anything of interest. One hundred feet away from the body, you stop to relieve yourself behind a small bush. Buried within, a staff has almost pierced the bush straight through. No wonder the reds didn't see it.

Through some strange psychic connection, the flight of reds return within moments of your discovery.  Determined to reclaim their staff, they immediately pinpoint your exact location and begin to swiftly descend in your direction.
The gate to the ice giants' citadel is heavily guarded.
You find a scrap of bloodstained paper blowing in the wind.  It reveals the location of a cave leading into the ice giants' compound.
Two men are actively engaged in a drunken brawl.  One is dressed in unusually fine clothes.  The other is dressed in a nondescript fashion.  You are unable to determine his class or social station.

Even though the men are drunk, they are   performing skilled hand-to-hand combat.  An exuberant crowd gathers round egging the men on. Bets are being placed. The man in fine dress is referred to as Clevis. You discover that the other is named Maxim.

With a major lunge, Maxim gets in a massive blow to the head. Clevis crumples to the ground. His head is gashed open on a razor-edged rock.  Townsfolk rush to Clevis's aid, but it's too late. Clevis is dead.  The highly charged crowd erupts into riot!

Captain Stillwater and guards arrive to enforce order. The captain sees Clevis lying motionless and rushes to his side. Shocked to find Clevis dead, he angrily jumps up. Narrowly surveying the hushed crowd, he demands them to admit who killed his brother.

Captain Stillwater's penetrating gaze locks on your presence amid the crowd.  His eyes pierce through you with a blazing intensity. "You there!  Why didn't you put a stop to this?  Your presence here proves my suspicions."

"Seize them! I will see their bodies swing from the yardarm tonight!"  Confusion and shouting breaks out. Determined to apprehend you, several armored men immediately begin to thrust their way through the crowd.

You step in and break the fighters apart.  Blood trickles down Maxim's cheek.  He sneers in your face. "You should choose your friends more carefully, outlanders!  You haven't seen the last of me!" He wrests his body from your grip and angrily stalks off.

Clevis eyes you harshly. "Strangers! You  have no right to interfere!  I shall see that my brother brings an end to your meddling!"  Accompanied by several supporters, Clevis irately sprints off to find his brother.

The man in charge of the guard is Clevis.  As soon as you are outside the town's protective walls, the gate is bolted shut.  Clevis gloats gleefully from a high lookout point and shouts, "Do not come back, filthy vermin! We will deny you entrance!"

You are walking past a building.  A man suddenly leans out one of the windows and motions to you.  "Hail!  I am Stellan, a friend of Maxim's.  We don't forget our friends here."  He tosses you a small pouch and quickly shuts the window.

The man in charge of the guard is Clevis.  He clasps your hands in a show of friendship.  "Hail, my good friends.  I see that you are setting out for the wilderness.  Wait a moment."  He enters the guardhouse and brings out a small satchel.
You open the satchel. Inside is a jar of foul-smelling goo.  "Take this powerful ointment with you. This salve is useful for healing.  It will aid you in your journey.  Farewell and take care."

There's a tap on your shoulder. Turning around, you confront Maxim.  He obnoxiously leers in your face. "So, you're still here! Too stupid to leave town, huh? Think you can just push others around? I'm gonna get you for helping Clevis earlier."

Maxim pulls out a small statuette, tosses it to the ground, and speaks an incantation. The statuette transforms into a living mystical creature. Startled, you discover that several of Maxim's lackeys have joined him. Where did they come from?

"Thank you, stranger.  I shall not forget your kindness. I must seek shelter and rest now.  My foe will be bitter over this defeat, and I must be prepared to meet and outwit any future engagements.  Good day."
You storm into the commander's quarters.  He is accompanied by half a dozen of his strongest warriors and a visiting party of ice giants.  They perceive you as a threat and quickly attack.

The deaths of the commander along with the visiting ice giants incites chaos. Several giant sub-chiefs argue for control of the citadel.  Unity disintegrates.  Bitter skirmishes break out among the forming factions.   No one pays you any attention.
In the corner is a large silver plated chest.
A magical bolt of energy erupts from the chest and strikes the would be thief.
You have opened the chest.  It contains several items of great worth.
A trio of beasts guard the door.  They perform their duty with vigor.
A locked door.  The sounds of many voices can be heard from the other side.  You cannot make out the conversation.

The door swings open easily. You confront a large group of giants. Your attention is immediately drawn to their durable, well-built weapons. Fortunately, you have caught the giants off guard. They are unable to summon reinforcements.
The door swings open to reveal a large group of giants. Weapons are drawn.

With ebbing strength, a gold dragon wildly defends itself against two red dragons. The dead bodies of several reds already litter the area. The gold has fought brilliantly, but it will not survive this last match unless you intervene. Do you?
Gold dragons are one of the few dragons that seek to spread goodness throughout the Realmz.  You rush to aid the gold in its fight against evil.

The gold dragon is badly wounded but still alive. After a brief rest, it accumulates enough strength to cast a magical healing spell. Rising to its full majestic height, it looks down and speaks in a deep, booming voice. "Thank you, good people. I...

would have perished if not for your bravery. My name is Vestron. Many months ago, I was out one morning when the cruel reds raided my mountain home. They abducted my mate and our young ones. I have been searching for them ever since.

Several times I have gotten close to getting my family back.  Every time I was severely beaten down by a horde of reds. It would give me great pleasure to bestow a gift on you for saving my life."  The gold dragon waves a clawed hand in the air.

A chest appears in thin air. The dragon  removes a small cloak from the chest and places it at your feet. "I offer you this valuable cloak. It has been in my family for over five generations. Please accept this fine gift as a token of my appreciation."

"Now I must be off. They have transferred my mate and young ones to a new site.  I must save them before it's too late.  If  you help me rescue them, I will reward you with an even finer gift."  Do you join the gold dragon?

"Excellent! You are brave and strong and will be a formidable ally. Climb upon my back. We shall fly to the enemies' holding.  Finally, I will be able to avenge the reds' cruel abduction of my family!

"The reds are located within these caverns.  This entry way is seldom used. We'll rest briefly before attacking.  I'll keep watch while you rest first.  When you're ready to venture in, return here. I'll be just inside the cave." The gold departs.
"Now that we have rested and renewed our strength, we shall fight these cruel reds and teach them to regret their evil ways!"
A group of red dragons is in the distance.   Do you wish to engage in combat?

You come across a massive iron door. You quickly remove the heavy iron rod that locks it in place.  A gold dragon is inside. She picks up a pair of eggs and rushes straight at you. You are blocking the doorway.

Without a word, the gold dragon seizes you and all your gear.  You are embraced in clawed hands the size of wagon wheels.  She swiftly races in the direction of the cave entrance. "We must escape before they discover my absence!"
"If they find me, I'm as good as dead.  I know too much of their plans.  We must escape and seal the cave behind us."  She soon reaches the entrance to the cave, spins around, and raises her palm.

She utters an incantation. The mountain starts to crumble. Instantly, the cave entrance is plugged with rock."They won't be able to follow for now. While I was being held prisoner, they used strong magical spells on my cell to render my magic useless."

"Tell me how you ended up accompanying my husband on this dangerous mission."  She listens in silence of her husband's fate.  She sighs thoughtfully, "Yes. That is just like Vestron.  He would promise the moon to save me."

"A pact made by my husband is one that I shall honor."  In the same manner as her mate, she waves her hand.  A chest appears, and she removes a small golden ring. "Take this. It is our most prized possession...

You have rightfully earned it and deserve to be rewarded for your bravery.  Now I must go.  I can't take the chance that a flight of reds will return.  My young must fall to no harm."  She rapidly ascends upward and flies off.

Just ahead of you, a large group of reds rest languorously.  Vestron whispers, "I can smell my mate beyond these wyrms.  Surprise will serve as our best weapon."  With a deafening roar, Vestron charges the reds.  Magical incantations spew from his lips.

In an intense clash with one of the reds, a claw bores through Vestron's chest and perforates his heart.  Vestron attempts to heal himself with magic, but it is too late. Life begins to drain from his body even as the words of healing pass his lips.

Willingly, Vestron accepts his fate. Death is worth his family's freedom. He begins to choke on his own blood. Quickly, you kneel down and lift his head slightly. He struggles to thank you for all your help. Vestron's eyes take on a glassy, vacant stare.
In the distance, some red dragons lie sunning themselves on the warm rock.  Do you attack them?

You come across a small temple.  Extremely obese friars waddle to and fro.  Their robes bear the evidence of permanent stains from too many greasy, heavy meals. "Children! You have bolstered our town's defenses. What can we do for our new heroes?"
Several creatures are traveling as a group along the shoreline.  Do you wish to attack them?
A group of giant spiders desire you for their next juicy meal.  You are far enough away that you could outrun them and escape.  Would you like to attack them?

Every tree in the valley is wrapped in webs.  Dead animal remains have been haphazardly thrown about the area.  Their carcasses look like dried plums, shriveled and drained of all fluids.  Giant spiders have infested this forest.
You spy movement in the distance.  Using sticky silken strands, several spiders  swiftly wrap three large bipeds.  Do you wish to rescue these poor creatures?
While the spiders are occupied, the three bipeds easily escape their sticky prisons.  It was a mistake to permit their release.

These wandering forest creatures have unknown motives. Their lives and actions are totally controlled by their creator's whims and desires. You feel ominous misgivings about what these creatures may be capable of. They seem to lack any sense of ethics.
A door has been carved into the trunk of a great tree.  Do you wish to enter?

You come upon a Greckle.  The odd creature has the body of a man but the hind legs of a goat.  The faun is resting soundly in a plump, cushioned bed. The mattress appears to be made from spiders' venom sacks stuffed with leaves.  What do you do?

As you slide your blade along the creature's throat, its eyes pop open. The involuntary reflex is disconcerting. Upon the faun's death, a magical hiding spell terminates revealing a secret opening in the tree wall. You discover several interesting items.
Do you wish to use one of the lamps to set this tree ablaze? You could rid the world of its foul presence.
In an instant, the tree bursts into flame.  You desperately spring back as the tree threatens to explode from the intense heat.  Flaming shards of wood engulf you.

Flaming embers fill the air alighting on dry twigs and leaves. The entire forest erupts into a blazing inferno. Barely able to breathe and racked by coughing, you manage to escape the wildfire. You and everything you own is blackened by soot and tar.
When you play with fire, you get burned.  Help prevent forest fires!

It perceives that it's not alone. It turns and accusingly points at you. A sharp,  unintelligible word leaps from its mouth. You cringe as an unendurable whistling  permeates the air. Flesh golems respond to its summons and attack from the doorway.

The strange creature tremulously utters one last magical word. Its body and all of its possessions abruptly vanish from sight. You are left standing alone near a barren tree. Several flesh golems lie dead at your feet.

A wail of pain rings out from nearby. You round a small knoll. An ice giant cleric is interrogating a small human boy. The boy is unable to escape the brutal grip of a trolls powerful claws. This unfamiliar breed of troll appears to be quite vile.
The ice giant cleric has tortured the boy almost to the brink of death. Do you wish to save the boy?
During the melee, the small boy is trampled underfoot by the trolls' massive steel shod boots.  Little is left of the body.

You cautiously approach the gate to yet another giant citadel.  It seems to be heavily protected.  From your vantage point, a dozen stygian trolls appear to be on guard duty.  A few others are idly wandering about.
A mighty battle. You destroy the hinge pin on the gate. It can no longer serve as a shield from their enemies.

You arrive at a huge citadel. The strong odors of sulfur and burning braziers drift your way. The place is unusually quiet and still. An occasional fire giant can be seen walking about. You slip in with ease.
A large hole in the ground. You peer down into the opening and quickly pull back feeling somewhat nauseous. Something down there is emitting a very pungent odor.
A short distance away, the ground begins to swell.   Large snakes push their way out of the ground and begin to slither in your direction.
You discover that the hole serves as home for several enormous snakes. Not only are they about sixty feet long, their diameters are as thick as a Golden Yew tree.
You have met with some success.  All your noise has attracted attention.  Alas, the attention is not coming from what dwells underground.

An old shack. Although somewhat bare, the place is warm and clean. At present, nobody is home. A log is smoldering in the fireplace, and a plate of mystery meat sits half-eaten on the wooden table.  It's aroma suggests seafood. Do you go inside?

You wait for over an hour. Your lookout  finally spots a portly old woman sitting atop a large wagon. The wagon is slowly being pulled closer by four ponderous beasts. It is heavily weighted down by the contents of six large wooden crates.

As the beasts pulling the cart draw near, they pick up your scent and begin to kick and snort. The old woman casts a spell to determine what is causing their uneasiness. She stiffens and eyes the shack warily. She is aware of your presence.

She cracks a whip, and the beasts charge into the clearing. The wagon careens out of control. The woman jumps out just before it tips over and spills its load. The crates smash open upon hitting the ground. The terrified beasts break from their harness.
You are drawn into a chaotic battle against two ponderous beasts, six giant crabs, and a portly old woman.
An intense search reveals a false stone above the fireplace mantel.  You pull the stone out and discover a small fortune of gold and magical items.
The place burns quickly.  In a matter of minutes, there is nothing but a heap of ashes.

A vibrant tree stands alone in the middle of a barren, rocky plain. The tree's healthy dark green foliage is striking and attractive amid this barren wilderness. There are no dead leaves or signs of insect damage.
You spot a patrol of fire giants. Do you ambush them?

You run into a lost patrol of human soldiers.  They are hastily making covert arrangements to ambush a large fire giant patrol.   Although surprise will be on their side, the fire giants heavily outnumber the humans.  Do you join them?

The patrol's commander is gravely wounded. He refuses aid. "My gods forbid  aid if it only serves to prolong the inevitable. I must accept that my time has come. Grant my dying wish. See that my slain men be buried with honor and dignity."

The distant sounds of battle seize your attention. You rush to find the source.  Back-to-back, a tight cluster of dwarves are desperately trying to defend themselves. They are surrounded on all sides by a fire giant patrol. Do you want to get involved?

The wounded leader of the dwarven patrol  speaks. "We have been searching for a lost patrol of humans. Years ago, during a winter storm, a pioneering group of humans found themselves lost in our mountains. They almost starved to death..."

"We nurtured them to health and set them up with food, clothing, shelter, and other necessities. To repay our generosity, they agreed to remain and work for three years. After this period of time, many chose to stay. One group never came back from...

a routine patrol. While searching for them, we were horrified to discover that our mountains are again teeming with giants. Since the giants have returned, I fear the worst for our human friends. I must return home to inform our chief."

You are nearing a crossroads in the tunnel. Suddenly, you are ambushed on all sides. You were unaware that a large tribe of orcs had set up a temporary encampment at this crossroad. Their sentries provided them with advance warning of your approach.

A crossroad is up ahead. You pause. The tunnel floor bears distorted footprints that could have been produced by steel shod boots. You have also discovered discarded litter. The evidence hints that the tunnel may be frequented by orcs.

A roughly hewn opening has been hacked into a side of the main chamber. It leads to a much smaller room. Intricate runes have been scratched into the dust. The tribe shaman must have inscribed them. They appear to be a warning to stay away.

A small group of orc warriors guards the cave entrance. They do not bother to waste time interrogating you. They quickly attack. From the cliffs overhead, a squad of archers loose a volley of arrows. The archers then climb down to join the fray.
Several guards stop you at the gate. "Begone, intruders! Baron Vlad sees no one. If you do not leave immediately, you shall pay with your lives." Do you attack them?
"As you wish! All forces, attack on my signal!" A tremendous deep boom instantly shatters the peace.

The clash of metal upon metal fills the air. Commands, agonizing screams and shouts of warning entangle together. A gate opens from the citadel beyond. Reinforcements from within pour forth to repel the attack.

An angry madman perches atop one of the battlements and screams at you. "You'll never see the inside of these walls! I'd destroy this fortress before ever yielding to you! Leave now or suffer eternal damnation!" More troops pour from the gate.

The madman soon bursts out of the gate. He's dressed in fine armor and brandishing a shimmering magical weapon. Along with his personal contingent, he plans to battle face-to-face. He eyes you wildly. "You should have left while you had the chance!"

Baron Vlad lies on the ground. Soon he will be dead. His body is already drenched by the blood of several gaping wounds. Struggling fretfully, he turns his face towards his mighty fortress and whispers, "My home... I cannot let it be stolen from me."

He pulls forth a small necklace from around his neck and smashes it. A low rumble sounds from deep within the fortress. Moments later, the castle is being blown apart by massive explosions. The entire mountain is vibrating. You fall to your feet.

Most of the Baron's servants and a few of his soldiers were still inside the fortress. Your skin crawls as horrible screams come from within. The castle walls are flying apart in all directions. The stones have become hurtling deadly missiles.
The entire castle has been uprooted and destroyed. A deep steaming crater and immense hunks of rock dot the landscape.  Baron Vlad is dead.
The door opens. Massive, hairy-knuckled hands grab you and pull you inside.  Before you can speak, you are thrust into furious combat with a large group of giants.

Honest Buttafooco's place lies in ruins. You question a passerby. Apparently, Buttafooco was under Baron Vlad's protection. When Vlad died, he took what he could and hastily fled. Looters pilfered everything else and burned the place to the ground.

You come upon a clearing in the woods. A glorious mansion has been built here. How peculiar! The mansion appears to have no windows of any kind. You wonder if the owner has some strange, morbid fear of the sun. Do you enter?
You find a considerable amount of gems.

A well-decorated room. The stylish furniture has been carefully arranged. Several creatures sit in the corner. Instead of mouths, they have squirming tentacles. Suddenly, you are hit by a forceful psychic blast. You become totally disorientated.
A tiny velvet pouch sits on a small table of polished zebra wood. You open the pouch and find a delicately fashioned gold ring inside.

Two Anti'Ids feed on the mind of some unfortunate creature they have captured. At your arrival, they manipulate the creature by infusing it with deceptive mental messages. It suddenly believes that you are a deadly enemy. All three attack you.

This door cannot be opened from the inside. Several hobgoblins have been imprisoned in the room beyond. The hobgoblins' eyes are glazed over. They  seem unaware of their surroundings. Do you wish to attack them?
They must be under some sort of mental control. They have been worked hard and have not been provided with adequate rest or nourishment. It appears that they are being used as slave labor.
Several Anti'Ids are gathered around a table.  They are arguing heatedly over a map.

You take the map.  The Anti'Ids have created a secret tunnel.  They now have access to a citadel of hill giants.  From their arguing, you gather that they intend to capture the giants for use as food.
The cavern complex dead ends here. You have no choice but to turn back. Several undead have moved in behind you and are blocking any means of escape.  You have no choice but to battle your way out.
The group was being controlled by a  mummy.  You unwrap the mummy to ascertain the creature's true identity.  Its eye sockets are stuffed with gems.
You wander into an unsavory part of town.  Assassins assault you.
You find a large brass key on one of the bodies.
This is the headquarters of the thieves' guild. The thieves are well aware of your approach and are already in their defensive positions.

Something is here. The wooden floor sounds slightly different when you step on it. You kneel. The boards have not been nailed down. They lift up easily. A large chest, heavily chained to an immense block of cement, is wedged in the dirt.
The chest is protected by magic. Spells successfully ward off all attempts to open the chest.
Enter the registration code as it appears on the second line of the form we sent you.
"Ah, our heroes have returned!" Lord Oswald's excitement swiftly fades as he listens to you briefly summarize your quest for the axe. He is distressed that you are not yet able to return it to him.

"Ah, our heroes have returned!" Lord Oswald greets you warmly. He then listens intently to all your stories concerning the reclamation of the Axe of Ashblet. "Well done, my friends! Your loyal service shall be rewarded generously."

"Ah, our heroes have returned!" Lord Oswald listens to an account of your exploits but grows steadily impatient. He suddenly stops you in midsentence. He is concerned over your failure to return the Axe of Ashblet to the dwarven kingdom.

"I need not remind you of the importance of this task. You must try again!" Before you can even open your mouth to respond, the guards efficiently whisk you out the door. Once again you set off to reclaim the famed axe of the dwarves.

Lord Oswald speaks. "Good people! Today you have done a great deed.  With the dwarves as our allies, we now stand a chance of surviving the forthcoming onslaught. For your devoted service, I bequeath you these fine gifts.

"Rest for awhile. The future requires much fortitude. I must leave at once to consult with the king. A meeting must be arranged with the dwarves without delay. We'll have to combine our forces in an effective manner and plan battle strategy."

"We must return the axe to the dwarves as soon as possible. This mission is of vital importance. Much is at stake. You are my best choice to deal with this highly sensitive matter. I trust that you will succeed in carrying out this task."

"Skill, courage and astuteness will be needed on this expedition. The secret location of the dwarven nation was known only by a few of my former servants. The knowledge died along with them. I am confident that you will locate it."

"When this mission is completed, you will be magnificently rewarded. As soon as you feel you have rested adequately, you must set off to deliver the axe to the dwarves. We cannot afford to wait long, or it will be too late."

"Baron McReese is in charge of  operations against enemy fortifications.  He is based in a mansion on the other side of town. I shall send a runner to notify him of your impending arrival. He will provide you with further instructions."
You arrive at a heavily guarded mansion. This must be the headquarters of Baron McReese, head of military operations against enemy fortifications. The guards escort you inside under a watchful eye.

The Baron stands over six and a half feet tall. His taut body is all muscle. He is presently poised over a map planning military strategy with several generals. At your arrival, he breaks away and strides over to greet you. He is a shrewd, concise man.

He pins you under his penetrating gaze. "I am Baron McReese. Under the king's authority, I am coordinating all efforts to destroy enemy fortifications. The outlook is grim. Even with all troops at my disposal, I can't mount a direct attack on...

an enemy stronghold. My troops are constantly engaged in defending small towns and villages from incessant raiding. We now hope to destroy the fortresses by relying on the surreptitious support of small groups of mercenaries like yourselves.

The giants have three main fortresses along with several strongholds. All frontal assaults have failed. So far, they've been able to outnumber our forces and hold out indefinitely. We are now relying on small bands of mercenaries. Unlike large forces,...

they may be able to covertly infiltrate giant fortifications and destroy the enemy from within. If you succeed in disrupting any of the giants' fortresses or strongholds, you will be generously compensated. The king has set aside a substantial...

cache of wealth and magical artifacts to reward those who meet with success. Victors over the giants can report back to me to receive their due. I wish you the best of luck. Good day." You are summarily dismissed.
A subordinate of Baron McReese listens to your exploits with mild interest.

Baron McReese is profoundly impressed by your elimination of the hill giant fortress. "We had attempted several frontal assaults, but they were dismal failures. This is an immense loss for the giants. You'll be substantially rewarded for this coup."

Baron McReese is pleased with your success at eliminating the ice giant fortress. "We had lost all contact with a small village on the other side of the rift mountains. Their relatives will be happy to know that many of the villagers have survived."

Baron McReese is overcome by the news of your destruction of the fire giant fortress. "Nothing can stop us!  We have won!  To reward you for your heroic service, the king shall grant you land and servants.  You will be dubbed Holy Knights of Vestguard!

The baron turns to his right-hand man. "Send a runner to inform the king of this mighty turn of events!  Summon all the garrisons!  We will rally and march forth to expunge any remaining giants!  Any possibility of them regrouping must be eradicated!

Armor-clad warriors shout and jump about like toads on a hotplate in an effort to carry out the baron's orders. Cheers of victory rise up. Horns blare. Troops hurriedly converge together from all directions.
You are standing in a small foyer.   Numerous ice giants begin to emerge from a room just east of you.
Giant guards are alerted by the discordant clash of dissension. They converge on the foyer from all directions. You are quickly surrounded.

A group of giants are seated around a large marble table.  From your hiding place, you overhear them talking.  They are considering asking the fire giants for aid in assaulting a nearby human village. A sudden, tense silence takes over the room.
An old, withered giant in flowing blue robes points in your direction. "Seize them!" The guards immediately jump up from the table.

A burly-looking warrior barks orders to his men to charge immediately. Those who fail will be beheaded. This little incentive appears to have quite an effect. The warrior's troops appear strikingly amoral and vicious.
You sift through the papers on the table and find an interesting map. You also discover a leather pouch containing a heavy ornate necklace.
A mage takes advantage of your reluctance to attack. A spell is cast that will increase the opposing warriors' success at slaying.

"Hold! A human this bold may be worth hearing out." You ramble in attempt to stall for time. Meanwhile, your thoughts race on how to outdo your rival. An intense realization occurs. Your stall tactic is being exploited to advance your opponent's position.
Within moments, reinforcements arrive to bolster the giants' numbers. They attack with increased confidence and vigor.
You hastily retreat from the room. A gong is beaten time and time again. The booming reverberations echo throughout the entire fortress and beyond. Everyone is now aware of the presence of intruders.
A few of the warriors mumble in disbelief, but they do not move to stop you.
The group of giants chortle amongst themselves.
You enter a large storeroom. Several heavy crates can be used to barricade the door.
A guard room. The guards are slack in performing their duties. Instead of patrolling, they are lying about playing bones and drinking. Upon your discovery, they quickly rise up to attack.
What luck! A copy of the patrol schedule is  in this room. You should be able to use this information to successfully avoid the giant patrols.
Without any warning, a magical field of energy bursts into full force. You are effectively repelled backward.
You hold the magical necklace aloft. The shimmering magical field gradually loses  power and fades away.

Flasks, beakers and glassware are spread over the tables in an elaborate setup. Tubes of glass piping connect much of the glassware together. Someone is very busy using this chemistry lab to create a variety of diverse, colorful concoctions.

A giant alchemist has just finished  injecting a puce-colored liquid into the buttocks of a large cave bear. Six more of the strangely docile beasts stand in line waiting to receive their injections. Do you attack?

The blood of the dead and wounded bears pours forth from their wounds in massive quantities. The blood emits a toxic vapor. What was in those injections? The fumes have a strong effect. Feeling faint and ill, you manage to stagger away for fresh air.
You enter a large room. It is sparsely furnished with an enormous set of table and chairs.

A huge glowing dog is chained to a post in the center of the room. At your presence,  it starts barking and foaming at the mouth. In a frenzy, it runs back and forth straining up against its chains. A door is on the other side of this round chamber.

A magical aura surrounds and protects the beast. All efforts at killing the beast by physical or magical means fail. Weapons and magical attacks pass harmlessly right through its body. If you move too close, you will surely die in its powerful jaws.
Your attempt to get past the beast  almost turns you into his personal supper bone. Those powerful jaws came much too close for comfort. You are forced to turn back.

At your wit's end, you finally try temptation. Dangling some meat from a stick, you hold it above the dog's head  egging him on until he has completely wrapped his chain around the pole. Too easy! You race through the door as the dog snarls furiously.
The hysterical dog strains against his chain and prances to the left and right. He manages to partly unwind it. The small room contains a valuable artifact.
You stand at the foot of an immense throne. It's chiseled from solid obsidian. The surface is as smooth as glass. Will someone sit in the throne?
You are transformed into a beautiful statue of solid obsidian.
An obsidian statue in the shape of a large crab sits on a slender white pedestal. Its eyes consist of two sparkling blue gems. Do you wish to take the gems?
The statue springs alive. It's ready to defend itself against all defilers.

Two large stone demons stand motionless before you. Their outstretched arms effectively block the entire hallway. If you want to pass by, you will have to get  them out of the way. Do you want to try and topple them?

You approach closer. The eyes of the statues are made of blue gems. A strange light seems to flare in them. Suddenly, they move into a defensive stance. They do not intend to let you through the corridor.

A sturdy door blocks your progress.  An elegant brass plaque has been set at eye level. You admire the artistically etched calligraphy. In bold, dramatic letters you read the name: Damius. A second line reads: High Mage of Qwint.

Fine tapestries decorate the walls. You suspect that they are quite valuable. The tapestries depict various battles between immense dragons, giants, and wispy, shadow-like women. Do you wish to take one?
You pull on a large tapestry. It depicts a pair of  wispy women and a gold dragon engaged in battle. The tapestry rips and collapses in a heap at your feet. The heap appears abnormally large.

In fact, the heap is growing! The tapestry is flung aside. A pair of wispy women float before you. You can see right through their shadowy bodies, but their dark eyes are black and opaque.  They pierce you with evil hatred.
"Foolish mortals!   We have long awaited for someone to release us. Damius forced us to endure this tapestry of imprisonment.  He shall pay for his folly. So shall you!"
Similar statues have been positioned in each corner of the room. The remaining statues animate to avenge their unearthly brother.

The commander advances forward to inspect the "mice" that have fallen prey to his trap. "Puny creatures! Who amongst you will consent to a duel with me? If one of you can defeat me in battle, all will be free to go.  The only condition is...
no one else may interfere. If you lose or refuse to take up my challenge, you will all die!" Will one of you consent to duel the commander?

You blink your eyes uncertainly.  Your gaze is drawn to the eastern wall.  It appears to be shimmering.  The floor shows several dusty footprints.  They all lead to the foot of the wall and suddenly stop.  No footprints lead away.
You discover a parchment lying on the passageway floor.  The parchment's wax seal remains unbroken.  Do you wish to break open the seal and read it?
The letters squirm about the page.  Finally, they stop moving, and you are able to read them.  It reads: "Fools!  Thieves!  Nobody is allowed in my secret chamber.  I will destroy you!"
The parchment bursts into a horrendous ball of flame.
The wall appears quite solid.  All attempts to pass through the wall to return to the other side are futile.

Large hairy beasts are caged inside a  holding pen.  You suspect that the giants use them as hunting animals. They are aggressive and temperamental. They move restlessly.  Their cramped quarters  engenders brief flashes of infighting.

Great flightless birds are packed into this cell. Although they're quite huge, a giant would consider them the size of a chicken. The giants are using them as livestock.  The immense birds gawk hungrily at you. They seem to think that you're dinner.
Loud clucking sounds come from up the hallway.  Feathers fill the air.
Further down the hall, the sounds of vicious snarling and growling passes right through a pair of large heavy doors.  The creatures inside must be quite savage.
A squad of combat troops is stationed here as guards.  They attack!

By pressing your ear to the door, you can make out the muffled voices of a pair of giants.  Together they poke fun and insult the bugbears' squad leader.  The bugbears are not amused.  Tempers are beginning to flare.  Do you wish to attack?

The bugbears' tempers get the best of them.  You hear the sound of swords being drawn. There are brief screams of agony.   After a moment, the door flings open revealing a large bugbear covered in blood.

It is shocked and surprised to see you standing there.  You see the bodies of two dead giants and a slain bugbear lying on the floor.  Seven smaller bugbears stand frozen about the room.  Do you attack them?

If other giants should discover these murders, the bugbears will surely be tortured and put to death. They rush past you and dash for the stairs.  The idea of pinning the blame on you for the giants' deaths never even crosses their simplistic minds.
Several distinct voices appear to be engaged in heated conversation on the other side of this door.  The discussion seems to revolve around guarding something.  Do you wish to attack?
A squad of bugbears bursts through a door from the west.  They investigate the source of the noise.
Flanked by commanders, a large giant emerges from the door to personally handle the problem.
A few mortally wounded giants and bugbears lie about the room.  Life oozes from wounds that will never heal.

Your gaze is drawn to the commanding presence of a large, polished oak desk. Fine antique chairs are arranged around it in a semicircle.  Giant-sized plate armor statues stand guard between bookcases of leather-bound books.

You search the desk and find a map displaying the location of a special iron pin.  Pulling this pin will result in a collapse of the entire fortress.  It was created to be used during an emergency situation requiring abandonment of the premises.
You ponder pursuing this course of action. If you can reach the pin and pull it, it would bring the entire structure down in a heap of rubble.
The chief's treasure trove.  If he had endeavored to use some of these items in  his battle against you, the battle could have swung in his favor.

The pin slides with ease from the floor.  As soon as it's removed, rumbling vibrations build upwards in a crescendo from deep below the ground.   Grit and mortar fall loose from the ceiling.  The fortress is doomed.  Time is short.  You are not safe here.

The map from the chief's desk pinpoints a  fake stone.  You locate the stone, pry it up, and discover a small pit.  A thick iron ring lies at the pit's bottom.  Closer examination shows that the ring is attached to a metal pin sunk into the ground.
The giants' inherent warlike nature takes control.  Their commander specifically ordered them to let you go if your champion was successful.  Instead, they disobey direct orders and attack.
The main structure of the castle is no longer able to support its own weight.  So ends the life of this once mighty fortress and all those still within.
The structure begins to crumble.  Large sections of wall fall all around.  Giants and bugbears run amok.  Desperate attempts are made to escape the fortress before its final collapse.

A closed door stands directly to the east.  A symbolic glyph has been carved into the marble floor just in front of the door.  The carving looks like it has been done recently.  You are unable to interpret the meaning of the glyph.

Suddenly, the glyph explodes throwing small pieces of marble about the room.  The pieces form into hideous creatures with gaping mouths of sharp teeth.  With shrill, piercing screams, they bear down on you.
The glyph glows with an intense green light.
You do not touch the glyph. You successfully pass by it without incident.
You depart from the fortress' main floor and begin to ascend stairs.  They lead upwards to the fortress' only tower.
You are at the entrance to the ice giant fortress.  Off to the southwest, your vision is able to discern a small town that appears to be inhabited by humans.  Do you wish to enter the fortress?

You smell smoke.  It drifts from deep within the forest.  You seek out the source of the smoke and come upon a trio of old hags.  The three hover attentively over a large iron pot.  Their mixture emits an evil, foul odor.  The three must be witches.
Do you wish to destroy the kettle and its contents?   OR   Do you wait to see what will happen when it is finished cooking?

You roll the pot off its legs and spill the sickly contents onto the grass.  An evil  abomination, half man and half undefinable creature, emerges.  The creature is covered in smelly mucus.  A large gem is embedded in its chest.
The three witches escape onto a hidden dirt path back into the forest.  They quickly disappear from sight.  Do you attempt to follow them?

After about twenty minutes, the pot begins to shake violently spilling some of its contents.  A large sword-wielding creature emerges.  It disdainfully surveys the compound.  The glowing eyes seem to penetrate through everything.
You manage to travel only a few paces down the dirt path before you are  assaulted by magic.  When the dust clears, you are confronted by the three witches along with two large sword-wielding brutes.

The witches cast a spell over the beast.  Its eyes glaze over in a state of apathy.  It now appears willing to obey their every whim.  From a nearby pile of stuffed burlap sacks, the witches drag out a dead human body.  They lay it flat on the ground...

and plunge a dagger into the chest.  Two of the witches mumble a strange prayer to an unknown god.  A large gem appears from thin air.  They thrust the gem into the corpse's chest.  The body is then placed in the pot, and the ritual begins anew.

Suddenly, the newborn brute spots you hiding among the bushes and lets out an enraged roar.  Similar brutes immediately emerge from a dirt path behind the witches.  The witches and brutes join forces and attack you.

Three fire giants are drilling a squad of stygian trolls in the fortress courtyard.  One of the trolls spots you.  He bellows out a sharp cry of alarm.  The exercises come to an abrupt halt when the others become aware of your presence.

You enter a large foyer.  The walls are lined with wooden pegs.  All are heavily laden with cloaks and ponchos.  Muddy boots of endless shape and variety  clutter the floor's edges.  Several giants and minotaurs mill about the congested room.
A squad of minotaurs guards this hallway.
Mass quantities of barrels have been stacked and stored in this room.  You pry the lid off one barrel to determine its contents.  The barrel is filled to the brim with oil.
What a mess!  You are now standing in two feet of oil.
The huge amount of oil in this room could be a potentially explosive fire hazard.  Thoughts of caution and danger suddenly become horrible reality.
If the explosion does not kill you, the collapse of the fortress will.  The entire fortress is ready to explode.   Tons upon tons of rock shall be your undoing.
You set fire to the string that protrudes from the firesticks.  Sparks fly as it slowly burns.  You watch in a state of edginess.  It will not take long.
A thunderous boom racks the citadel.  Its very foundations tremble in alarm.  Upon the firesticks' explosion, burning oil erupts from the room and spreads throughout the fortress.
A patrol approaches.  Do you wish to attack them?

You open the door to this cell.  Half a dozen humans sit huddled on the floor in chains.  By the looks of them, they have not been allowed to bathe or eat very often.  Do you free them so that they may attempt an escape?

They thank you for the opportunity.  All rush out the cell door.  Within moments, you hear a stygian troll barking orders to a squad of minotaurs commanding them to attack the human escapees.  Alarm gongs begin to sound off all over the area.
This cell displays the bodies of several dead dwarves chained against the wall.

Six elves are chained to a wall.  Six orcs are chained to the wall directly opposite them.  It's obvious that they haven't been here long, since they're all in very good health.  They offer to pledge their lives to you, if you free them.  Do you?

You spare them some equipment so that they're partially armed.  Just as you're about to leave the cell, a large patrol of stygian trolls passes by.  One looks through the cell door peephole, notices the empty chains, and alerts his comrades.
You help the wounded as much as possible.  They're aware of the importance of your mission and beg you to continue without them.

This must be the living quarters of a high level giant warrior.  Many pieces of fine polished armor and weaponry embellish the room.  You conduct a hasty, overall search of the premises.  A large iron chest contains some items of interest.
One of the weapons on the walls glows with an intense brilliance.  Such luminosity can only come from STRONG magic.

A pair of enchanters stand behind the door.  Startled, they abruptly finish capping a small bottle.  One immediately turns toward a back room and cries out in alarm.  He attempts to warn others of your presence and call for help at the same time.

You make short work of the enchanters.  Caught off guard, they stood little chance against such seasoned adventurers.  The giants in the back room are a different matter.  They're experienced warriors and were warned of your presence ahead of time.

The troops you just slew were quite well- to-do.  Just prior to their fateful encounter, they had been enjoying a game of bones.  A heaping pile of gold and gems sits abandoned in the midst of a gaming circle.

You enter a magnificent wizard's lab.  The elaborate equipment and intricate set up looks advanced beyond your wildest imagination.  Electricity bounces among strange bronze globes.  Liquids portraying every color of the rainbow...
boil in beakers of every shape and size.     While you stand awestruck by your surroundings, the lab's intelligent creator happens to be staring intently at you.

Your attention suddenly focuses on a giant enchanter.  He is surrounded by strange creatures in a far corner of the lab.  You are conscious of the fact that they are engaging in conversation.  Their means of communication is...

telepathy. Its nature is so strong, you can almost feel their words in your mind.  You  suddenly feel compelled to stand very still and quiet.  Within moments, you regain your wits.  However, it's too late.  You have fallen victim to a mind attack...
of the most subtle kind.  Your delay has given your enemy the upper hand.  They assault you with an all-out mental barrage.

You pause at a large circular room.  A fire giant stands with his back to the door screaming at a group of giants who have their eyes deferentially fixated on the floor.  He severely berates their failure to find and dispose of the intruders.

In addition to the commander, there are fully two dozen giants in this room.  One of the lower ranking giants, young and foolish, risks a glance upward at the commander.  He spots you and shouts an alarm.

You step into a well-furnished room.  Weary and haggard, a giant enchanter sits sobbing at a table.  He hears you enter the room and stops to wipe his runny nose.  "Go ahead!  Kill me!  I don't care.  I have lost everything to that devil Utris."

"A few weeks ago, I was the master enchanter for Chief Blackthorne.  One of my experiments on a wild creature failed.  The beast ran amok and killed the chief's son.  Never one to miss an opportunity, Utris denounced my work.  Chief Blackthorne...

stripped me of my title, destroyed all my work, and appointed Utris the new Master Enchanter.  I swear I shall destroy Utris or die in the attempt.  If you will help me, I shall reward you with my last worthy possession."

"Good!  Together we shall show Utris what it means to fail.  Come with me!"  He leads you to a secret laboratory that Utris has set up to conduct his experiments.  "Whatever you do, do not look him in the eye.  He is very adept in...
ways of the mind.  I have no doubt that he used these mind control skills on Blackthorne to secure his appointment as the new master.  Now!  Let us deal Utris the failure he so richly deserves."

With the aid of your new friend, you are able to sneak up on Utris.  He is conducting a vile experiment on a small lamb.  The animal's skull has swollen to an immense size.  A group of Anti'Ids helping Utris, gaze at the large brain...

of the helpless animal as you might eye a duck that has been roasted to perfection.  You attempt to swallow your revulsion at the foul experiment.  You burst into the room more determined than ever to slay Master Enchanter Utris.

You attend to your wounded friend.  "My friends, I must fulfill my promise.  This item will serve you faithfully."  He pulls a small human-size dagger from his belt.  Though it is too small for him to wield, it fits your hand well.
