He does nothing to stop you.  Except for a map revealing the location of a secret lab, your search produces little of interest.  Upon this impudent violation of his inner sanctum, the former master enchanter heart brokenly abandons the room.
He puts up no struggle and quickly succumbs to your ruthless blades.
A minotaur rests on a large cot.  He sits up as you enter.  Groggy from sleep, he is not totally aware of what's going on.  Do you rush him before he can regain control of his wits?
You hear the old enchanter yell warnings about intruders in the fortress.  A squad of minotaurs shows up to investigate.

Clearing its head, the large minotaur quickly reaches under its cot and pulls out a large sack of yellow crystals.  The minotaur grabs a handful, scatters them about the floor, and utters some strange words.
The room is filled to the brim with arrows and quivers.  A jolly whistling tune carries over from the other side of a small wall that divides the room in two.

The castle fletchers sit on sturdy stools  busily whistling and creating additional arrows.  At your approach, they take up bows and nock arrows.  Before you can take cover, they let fly.  The magical arrows resemble flaming comets.

This barracks houses the main force of minotaurs.  There are about twenty or so troops here.  They all appear to be sleeping soundly.  A large door is on the other side of the room.  Do you make an attempt to get to the door?
The minotaurs from the barracks have been hot on your trail.  You must have left a sign of your passing.  Now they have caught up to you.
You stumble on a patrol of fire giants.
Numerous giants feast ravenously at long wooden tables.  With eager anticipation, they shove tables and crockery aside to make room for battle.

The smelly, unsanitary kitchen is deserted.  Pots of foul gruel sit abandoned on a counter.  Grease and dried bits of food coat the kitchen surfaces.  The door can be bolted from within.  This room may serve as a potentially safe place to rest.
"Why, I'm here to keep the ants out!   Would you like some poison to keep them critters away?"

You peek into a large pot and find it stuffed with giant ant body parts.  A thick mold is swiftly growing over the dead ants.  Inside one of the cabinets, you locate two separate vials.  You have a choice of Ant Repellent versus Ant Poison.  The vial...
labeled Ant Repellent reads, "Drink to repel ants."  An iron key lies next to the vials.

You behold a vast battle.  Many bone crabs struggle for their lives against an endless torrent of giant ants.  The crabs crush dozens of the ants, but they're slowly succumbing to these en masse mindless kamikazes.  Do you enter the fray?
A long sword is embedded in the carapace of a dead crab.  The crab was stabbed  long ago and the weapon was never retrieved.  It's likely that the owner of the sword did not survive the engagement.
You encounter a group of tormented souls. They wish to reclaim what you have taken.
You are approached by a patrol of Baron Vlad's troops.  They order you to leave the area.  If you refuse, they threaten to use force.  Do you attack them?
You are attacked by a patrol of Baron Vlad's troops.

The portly priest who runs this temple is rude and curt.  He informs you that their small, peaceful community is  self-sufficient and wants nothing to do with worldly outsiders.  He asks that you leave this house of worship.
A stout priest spots the Tomb of Shalizar jutting from one of your sacks.  "Ah, fine people!  I see that you have recovered one of my lost scriptures.  Would you care to return it to me for a price?"

You come upon a small krise child.  The trembling child huddles in a dark, dank corner of the cave.  You kneel down in friendship.  The child cries that it wants to go home, but it is afraid of the great beast.  Do you help the child get home safely?

The scaly little critter leads you deep into the tunnel.  Suddenly, it slips out of sight.  You search around the next bend and are immediately attacked by a large party of krise.  They use large, trained cave lizards to aid them in battle.
Several of the krise possess large nets.  They apparently intended to capture you alive.
You traveled late into the night and finally made camp just outside the gates of the city of Northgate.  You awaken to a beautiful summer morn.  Eager to check out Northgate, you hastily break camp.

You have traveled the Realmz far and wide in search of adventure.  Rumors of trouble brewing in Northgate have irresistibly drawn you here.  Every seasoned adventurer knows that danger and treasure go hand in hand.
All hearty souls, prepare!  Polish your boots and sharpen those blades!  You are about to Assault Giant Mountain!
A well-stocked storeroom.
The fire sticks ignite setting off a tumultuous explosion.  In a roiling inferno, the fortress of the fire giants is totally obliterated.

You stand at the foot of a mighty fortress.  Raucous, booming laughter comes from within.  A giant emerges from a massive iron gate.  His approach is slow and deliberate.  His eyes speak of timeless age, but his body appears extremely powerful and alert.

"I am Lequtus, creator and master of all giant kin.  My children lie broken at your feet, and still you seek to destroy me.  I am aware of all your deeds, and you will pay dearly for the havoc you have caused.  You will know the vengeance of the master."

"For many years, I have lain in a dormant state.  I rested and gathered my strength until it was time to once again rise and set the Realmz free.  Your puny kind have defiled this majestic world for far too long."

"You have spread like an infectious disease, destroying all that you touch.  I, Lequtus shall set all to right.  The  prophesies of the gods shall be fulfilled."  The fiery speech comes to an abrupt end.  A warbling sound reverberates throughout the area.

Giants pour en masse through the massive iron gate Lequtus just emerged from.  They quickly form a skirmish line and begin to chant.  They do not speak in a giant tongue.  You are unable to interpret the meaning of this peculiar, rhythmic speech.
With a gesture from Lequtus, the entire force of giants rushes you with bold, vehement intensity.

Lequtus lies mortally wounded on the blood soaked ground.  "Fools!  You cannot destroy me!  The gods watch over me as if I were one of their own babes.  I may be forced to surrender this mortal shell, but my essence will live on."

"As before, hundreds of restful years will allow me to return and fight yet again for my rightful power.  Until then, the world will suffer for my absence."  Amid harsh laughter, his body and castle turn to dissipating smoke.  Only his clothes remain.

The good news reaches the king and you are sent for.  You personally relate the triumph over Lequtus and explain that the Realmz may now expect peace for the next several hundred years.  The king expresses gratitude and pride in your  achievements.
